items.t: Hundreds of Artex AI hacking tools found publicly exposed to the web
items.d: Security researchers found hundreds of servers hosting the penetration testing tool Artex exposed to the internet, allowing anyone access to the hacking tool.
items.x:
Security researchers found hundreds of servers hosting the penetration testing tool Artex exposed to the internet, allowing anyone access to the hacking tool.
Security researchers have discovered hundreds of copies of a Chinese-made AI hacking tool publicly exposed to the internet for anyone to access, potentially allowing outsiders to launch cyberattacks against unsuspecting targets.
The hacking software, called Artex, is an open-source autonomous penetration testing tool, meaning software that automatically probes computer systems for weaknesses, and it’s been linked to several cyberattacks since its public release in July. As open-source software, it’s free for anyone to download and run on their own servers, making it a popular tool for those who cannot access Anthropic or OpenAI’s most advanced cybersecurity AI models for discovering security vulnerabilities.

items.t: Meta introduces Spaces, a new way to collaborate with your Muse agent
items.d: Meta's Muse agents continue to get new features and integrations. Spaces promises to be a new way to interact with the AI helpers.
items.x:
Meta's Muse agents continue to get new features and integrations. Spaces promises to be a new way to interact with the AI helpers.
Meta recently launched its Muse agents — a new generation of cuddly agentic helpers. Now, the company has launched Spaces, a new way to communicate and collaborate with them.
As far as I can tell, Spaces are basically breakout conversations that revolve around a particular topic — although Meta refers to them as “custom experiences.” They live in the sidebar of the interface where you interact with your Muse agent. Clicking on the Space brings up the conversation, where Muse works towards a particular goal on your behalf.
For instance, if you wanted to plan a vacation, you could open a new Space focused on that particular project, and whenever you want to work on it with Muse, you would click to open that particular tab. Or, if you’re focused on collecting recipes for an upcoming family event, you’d open a new Space for that particular project.

items.t: How a Blue Wave midterm might reshape the AI industry
items.d: Democrats’ historic victories in this week’s U.S. midterm elections could also transform the tech industry. The public voted on 41 data center-related ballot measures on Tuesday — in all but one, the majority voted to impose more…
items.x:
Election week is already reshaping the AI data center debate. This week on Equity, we dig into the fallout, plus Canva’s layoffs, a $115B chip deal, and microdramas.
Democrats’ historic victories in this week’s U.S. midterm elections could also transform the tech industry.
The public voted on 41 data center-related ballot measures on Tuesday — in all but one, the majority voted to impose more restrictions on data center development. And even when data centers weren’t on the ballot directly, they were a major talking point, with newly-elected Democratic governors and congressmembers likely to support additional regulation.
On the latest episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast, Kirsten Korosec, Sean O’Kane, and Anthony Ha discuss what the election will mean for the tech industry moving forward — not just when it comes to data centers (which OpenAI is already trying to rebrand), but also increased government scrutiny of Big Tech.
Anthony Ha is TechCrunch’s weekend editor. Previously, he worked as a tech reporter at Adweek, a senior editor at VentureBeat, a local government reporter at the Hollister Free Lance, and vice president of content at a VC firm.

items.t: “Does Meta think we can’t read?” Meta abandons sketchy commercial terms update.
items.d: Meta won't force Facebook page owners to allow AI training on linked content.
items.x:
After weeks of backlash —and a failed attempt to quell it —Meta has indefinitely delayed plans to update its commercial terms and require Meta Business account users to allow extensive AI training on external websites linked on Facebook.
"We're pausing the ‌changes ⁠as we continue to engage with stakeholders and ​take ​our ⁠time to get this right. ​In the ​meantime, ⁠our existing terms remain in ⁠effect," a Meta spokesperson told Reuters.
Soon after Meta notified business account holders of the upcoming changes, legal experts warned Nieman Lab that the vague language could allow the company to ignore scraping preferences specified in robots.txt files and exhaustively crawl vast amounts of off-Facebook content for AI training. Since virtually every news publisher has a Facebook page, Nieman Lab sounded the alarm that Meta could potentially avoid millions in licensing fees if the TOS update happened as planned.

items.t: Could potential AI clones of GTA VI force a quicker official port?
items.d: A former Rockstar tech director thinks the developer is facing new time pressures.
items.x:
Yesterday, when reporting on emerging efforts to pipe the console version of GTA VI through a PC's DLSS-powered Nvidia GPU , we mentioned in passing that PC players could instead just wait for the AI-assisted decompilation port that will no doubt be coming in short order. Now, a former Rockstar tech director says he thinks that exact threat could cause the developer to work faster on the official PC version of its soon-to-release crime/lifestyle simulator.
Obbe Vermeij hasn't worked at Rockstar since 2009 , but in a new interview with Rock Paper Shotgun , he recalled how artists for the PC version of the original, top-down Grand Theft Auto were incensed when the console version squashed the game's 256-color textures down to 16 colors for the PS1 release.
"So it always has been that sort of awkward relationship between PC and the console," Vermeij said. "So in those days, it was like PC first and then console second, even though that didn't really make much sense for the sales, because the PlayStation versions sold way better."

items.t: Ramp data shows AI spending stalling just as Anthropic nears its IPO
items.d: AI usage keeps climbing, but spending has stalled. Price cuts and smarter cost controls among the biggest spenders could challenge investor assumptions about AI hypergrowth.
items.x:
AI usage keeps climbing, but spending has stalled. Price cuts and smarter cost controls among the biggest spenders could challenge investor assumptions about AI hypergrowth.
Companies are using more AI than ever, but they’re not spending more on it.
A new report from Ramp shows AI spending flatlined over late summer even as token volumes rose, a sign that price competition and savvier customers may be capping revenue for OpenAI and Anthropic. According to Ramp’s data, token spend only grew 1.5% across August and September. To compare, in July, it grew 42% from the previous month.
As Anthropic gears up for its IPO, the data suggests investors might be wrong to assume AI companies will keep growing at breakneck speed.
“Almost the entire spend on AI is from venture-backed, high-growth tech companies,” Ramp’s lead economist Ara Kharazian told TechCrunch.

Amazon said that the feature will roll out to millions of users in coming weeks.
Amazon is jumping on the currently most popular bandwagon for interacting with AI agents: texting. The company on Friday said it is launching a feature that lets customers chat with its Alexa AI agent over text messages to help them shop, much like you can with AI agents like Muse or Instinct.
The move comes after Amazon blocked Meta’s Muse from querying its site in September. The company is rolling the features out just before the start of the holiday shopping season.
The e-commerce giant said select U.S. customers will get a text asking them to enable the shopping feature. Those with access can text Alexa to shop on Amazon using natural language queries, spanning everything from searching for items, adding them to cart, and purchasing.
The text agent builds on the recent shopping-focused upgrades to Alexa, and so can manage lists, keep tabs on prices, search for items across the web, compare products, and check the status of orders.

items.t: ToyBlocks: A controlled world for robot learning and evaluation
items.x:
Robots are learning to fold laundry, sort parts, and handle unfamiliar objects. But those demonstrations are often rather narrow and don't explain what a robot has learned or why it fails.
To study a complex system, scientists often begin with a small, controlled environment, such as a petri dish or terrarium, where they can vary conditions and observe the effects. Robotics needs environments that make this kind of investigation possible—researchers should be able to change the training data or model design, repeat a test, and trace the cause of a failure.
Today we're introducing a framework for creating these environments; we call them FoundationWorlds. Each pairs a controlled, simulated world targeted at studying robotics in a specific environment with tools for automatically generating tasks and training demonstrations, as well as metrics for measuring a robot's behavior over time. Together, they provide a setting for studying questions such as how models improve as more training data becomes available, and how to best combine high-level reasoning with precise physical control.
Our first foundation world is ToyBlocks: an open simulation framework built around a robot arm and blocks on a tabletop.

items.t: Underdog shows off a 32MB speech model in new demo
items.d: Despite its small size, Underdog's new model can generate both speech and music.
items.x:
Despite its small size, Underdog's new model can generate both speech and music.
AI companies across the world are racing to make bigger and better models, but the problem is all of them need massive amounts of processing power. On the other end, some researchers and startups are creating smaller models that can run on edge devices, like your phone or computer.
One such startup, Underdog, has released a game built with its new voice model called Woof that’s only 32MB large.
The game features a room with a retro tech theme, a typewriter, and a CRT monitor. There is a desk lamp, which makes a sound when you click its switch. The intro warns users about “intrusive” cloud providers in the town — ostensibly a jab at cloud-based models.
We made a game for our new frontier text-to-speech model, Woof. 31.7 MB, so small that it runs in your browser Play the game on X… all voices are Woof. Defeat Darkcloud for an invite https://t.co/ImUFYDCBQG pic.twitter.com/tthHx7ZGBK
You can type anything on the typewriter using your keyboard, and the game will speak it back. You can also rotate the tuner to generate different kinds of music.
All of this works within the browser through Underdog’s speech generation model, which, the company says, can run on most devices without any internet connection.

items.t: Physicl raises $10M to make the digital world real enough for robots
items.d: Physicl is trying to solve the sim-to-real gap with a pipeline originally built to market goods online.
items.x:
Physicl is trying to solve the sim-to-real gap with a pipeline originally built to market goods online.
Alex de Vigan’s last business got swamped by the rise of generative AI, but now he’s betting the tech that team had built, a platform for creating tempting product renderings for e-commerce, can be re-purposed to make robots more useful.
His new venture, Physicl, has raised $10 million in seed funding from Inovia Capital to help world model designers and robot builders solve thorny training problems with more realistic simulations.
Founder and CEO de Vigan spent the last decade building nfinite, which made it easy for brands and retailers to create 3D models of their goods and display them online. The arrival of transformer-based AI models led that company to focus more on generative imagery, but de Vigan saw a new purpose for his team and the tech stack they’d built to faithfully render 3D environments.
“What we were super unique about doing in 3D, AI was going to replace, but something was missing in AI: its ability to understand, interact, and manipulate space and objects,” de Cigan says.

items.t: I watched a humanoid robot clean my apartment. It felt like a taste of the future.
items.d: I’m not the sort of person who typically pays for a house cleaner. I’m too frugal, and I kind of enjoy putting on a podcast and going to town on my tub with a Magic Eraser. But when I saw an X post about a new humanoid-robot cleaning…
items.x:
I’m not the sort of person who typically pays for a house cleaner. I’m too frugal, and I kind of enjoy putting on a podcast and going to town on my tub with a Magic Eraser. But when I saw an X post about a new humanoid-robot cleaning service in San Francisco, I immediately signed up for the waitlist. I wanted my apartment to feel like The Jetsons , even if just for an hour.
I was also motivated by journalistic interest. In order to ensure an authentic experience, I didn’t tell Tau Robotics, the startup behind the X post, that I was a journalist—though I did use my real name, so it’s possible someone looked me up. Tau’s long-term goal is to make autonomous cleaning robots a reality, but they’re not quite there yet: For now, the robots are piloted remotely by humans, who watch what’s going on via cameras mounted in the robots’ heads and wrists. As the robots clean, they collect data that Tau will use to train up their more independent descendants. Every counter successfully wiped and T-shirt successfully folded will help the models that power the robots learn to do better on the next go-round.
Because this data is so valuable to Tau, the company charges less for cleaning than one might expect for such a cutting-edge product.

items.t: Apple’s China AI partner has had a rough ride
items.d: Editor’s note: On Nov. 4, Apple Intelligence began beta testing in China, with Alibaba’s Qwen available in selected Siri, Writing Tools and Visual Intelligence experiences. The partnership crowns an unusually fast ascent for a model family…
items.x:
Edit or’s note: On Nov. 4, Apple Intelligence began beta testing in China, with Alibaba’s Qwen available in selected Siri, Writing Tools and Visual Intelligence experiences. The partnership crowns an unusually fast ascent for a model family launched in 2023. Hugging Face counted more than 2 billion Qwen downloads on its own Hub in the first seven months of 2026, well ahead of Google and Meta. But Qwen’s rise was anything but smooth: internal skepticism, fierce competition and senior departures shaped the model long before it became a global name.
Qwen’s path to Apple did not begin as the story of an inevitable champion.
Alibaba introduced Tongyi Qianwen in April 2023, months after ChatGPT jolted China’s technology industry into a race to build large language models. It soon began releasing model weights publicly, gradually making open source central to Qwen’s strategy.
Even inside Alibaba, Qwen was not the automatic choice . Some teams kept using Meta’s Llama well into 2024, while Fliggy and Alibaba.com later experimented with DeepSeek’s R1. The model had to win over its own company before it could win over the wider market.
Open source became part of the answer.

The company also increased free usage allowances and said it would continue adjusting resources to meet demand.
According to materials provided by Tencent, Hy4 ranked second among Chinese models on Artificial Analysis’ intelligence index, behind Kimi K3.1 Pro. It also ranked 13th overall and first among open-weight models on Agent Arena. Tencent cited an Artificial Analysis benchmark cost of about $0.78 per task.
Tencent released Hy4 on November 4 , adding visual understanding and expanding pre-training and post-training compared with its preview version. The company said the upgrade improved instruction following, long-context comprehension, and extended agent workflows. [TechNode reporting]

items.t: Cainiao Opens Its Global Warehouse Network as a Real-World Training Ground for Embodied AI
items.d: Cainiao is opening its global warehouse network to AI and robotics firms for real-world training, with 100+ test scenarios, and launched a three-day overseas delivery service for tech hardware.
items.x:
Cainiao, Alibaba's logistics arm, said on November 5 that it is opening its global warehouse network to industry partners as a real-world training, testing and deployment site for AI and embodied intelligence companies. The announcement came at an AI and embodied intelligence partnership event held at the Cainiao Smart Gateway in Hong Kong, according to IT Home and Sina Tech. Cainiao described the network as the world's largest real-world logistics training cluster for AI and embodied intelligence. The company also launched a three-day delivery service aimed at AI computing and robotics companies shipping overseas.
Cainiao is making dozens of industries and more than 100 proof-of-concept scenarios available to partners for joint development, training on physical robots and business validation. The scenarios cover warehouse picking, smart navigation and delivery, high-altitude inspection, security operations, air logistics and auto parts management.

items.t: Tencent Expands Hy4 Capacity Tenfold After WorkBuddy Demand Surge, Cites New Benchmark Rankings
items.d: Tencent has scaled Hy4's inference cluster tenfold after WorkBuddy users hit quotas on day one, and cites second place among Chinese models on Artificial Analysis.
items.x:
Tencent said on November 5 that it has expanded the inference cluster serving its Hy4 large language model tenfold after a surge in usage on WorkBuddy, its AI agent for office work, where many users hit their quotas on the model's first day of availability.
According to a notice from the Tencent Hy and WorkBuddy teams, the company has also raised free usage quotas and will keep reallocating resources as demand shifts. The teams cautioned that limits may still appear at peak times because of constraints on high-end computing capacity and concentrated demand. They suggested switching to other models such as Hy3, whose free access on WorkBuddy has been extended to 23:59 on November 15, or moving non-urgent tasks to the evening.
Tencent also cited the Intelligence Index that Artificial Analysis published on November 5, which ranks 724 models. Hy4 placed second among Chinese models, behind Kimi K3.1 Pro and ahead of Qwen3.8 Max and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash. The index combines evaluations spanning complex reasoning, coding, tool use, multimodal understanding, long-horizon planning and scientific problem solving.

items.t: Palo Alto Networks in talks to buy AI agent security startup Clutch for $500M
items.d: Clutch, backed by Lightspeed and SignalFire, was last valued at $85 million, according to a source.
items.x:
Clutch, backed by Lightspeed and SignalFire, was last valued at $85 million, according to a source.
Palo Alto Networks is in talks to acquire Clutch Security, a startup that secures AI agents’ access to company systems, for $500 million in cash plus additional milestone-based payouts, according to a person familiar with the discussions.
Three-year-old Clutch was last valued at $85 million when it raised a $20 million Series A round in January 2025, led by Lightspeed and SignalFire, according to our source. The startup is currently approaching $10 million in annual recurring revenue (ARR). That means the acquisition, if completed, would value Clutch at about 50 times its ARR, a standard way of pricing software companies.
Palo Alto Networks and Clutch Security did not respond to a request for comment. The Information was the first to report the acquisition discussions.
The high valuation is not an anomaly in a market increasingly focused on securing software against bad actors using AI to breach systems more easily.

items.t: China Unveils an AI Agent Identity Registry at Wuzhen as 20 Organizations Sign Self-Discipline Pact
items.d: An AI agent identity registration and resolution platform was unveiled at Wuzhen, while 20 organizations including Huawei, Alibaba and Tencent signed an agent self-discipline pact.
items.x:
An identity registration and resolution platform for AI agents was unveiled on November 4 at a World Internet Conference Wuzhen Summit forum on agent trust, interconnection and interoperability, IT Home and China Daily's Chinese-language site reported. At the same forum, 20 organizations including Huawei, Alibaba, Tencent, Xiaomi and Baidu released a self-discipline convention for AI agent development.
The platform is still being built out. According to the reports, parties at the national level are jointly constructing it to handle identity coding, cross-domain resolution and trusted interoperability, with operating platforms layered on top to host agent access and capability publishing. Rather than returning an answer with a block of written explanation, as photo-search homework apps typically do, the agent combines step-by-step teaching, follow-up questions and animated whiteboard drawings.
Youdao frames the product around a common frustration: students can read a worked solution and still not understand why an auxiliary line goes where it does in a geometry problem, or how to handle a function question once the conditions change. The company says the agent is meant to move students from understanding an answer to being able to solve similar problems on their own.
The tutoring flow has three parts. First, the agent hints at a direction before walking through the key derivations and calculations one step at a time, and it ends by naming the method used and the core concept the question tests. Second, students can stop at any step and ask follow-up questions, so the explanation adjusts to where they are stuck instead of running through a fixed script.
Third, the agent draws.

Google didn't see the backlash coming, but now that it's here, the search giant is clarifying what exactly its new policy means and what's changing.

items.t: Vera Delivers the Best of Both Worlds: Highest Throughput and Fastest Agents
items.d: AI agents do more than generate answers. They search for information, query databases, write and test code and take action. Each of those steps relies on a CPU, with agents moving between GPU reasoning and CPU execution throughout a task…
items.x:
AI agents do more than generate answers. They search for information, query databases, write and test code and take action.
Each of those steps relies on a CPU, with agents moving between GPU reasoning and CPU execution throughout a task.
As businesses put more agents to work, AI factories need CPUs that can execute those steps quickly and support many agents at once, all within the limits of available power.
What this means: AI infrastructure providers need to support more agents without making each one wait longer to get work done. And critically, AI factories are power limited. This means operators need to choose infrastructure that maximizes the work done for every watt.
Why it matters: NVIDIA Vera delivers both fast agent performance and high capacity per watt within a single CPU.

Justicz, who has a hobbyist’s interest in cybersecurity and previously found a vulnerability in the same codebase, told TechCrunch that he found this issue using GPT 5.6 Sol, released in July, through the AI maker’s Daybreak Blue, a program that gives cybersecurity defenders access to powerful frontier models.
“I literally just aimed ChatGPT at the same body of code and said ‘I found this bug previously that was fixed several years ago, please find bugs as bad or worse,’ and it came back in two hours with this,” Justicz said. “It’s extremely convoluted and hard for a human to find, but it works!”

items.t: Axiom Math wants to keep AI slop out of mathematics

items.x:
As AI floods math with unchecked proofs, Axiom Math is betting on verification. The startup’s AI agents just formally verified the Stacks Project, one of the field’s biggest libraries.
It feels like AI is cracking a new math problem every week. Last month, OpenAI released 719 manuscripts claiming solutions to some of the field’s hardest problems. Even the computer checks can slip. After years of AI slop, it’s fair to wonder whether math is next.
Axiom Math is betting math can avoid that fate, not by slowing down, but by standing on firmer ground. The $1.6 billion startup wants to build a verified foundation that AI agents can rely on to write software and, eventually, do science.
On Wednesday, the company announced it had formally verified the Stacks Project, one of the largest bodies of mathematics ever written by humans. Mathematicians often hold Stacks in rare regard — Columbia mathematician Peter Woit has claimed there’s “nothing else really comparable,” comparing the project to “the famous Bourbaki books,” a series that rebuilt math from its foundations in the 20th century.
Woit’s Columbia colleague Johan de Jong started the Stacks Project in 2005 as an open source reference.

items.t: More Performance From Every Byte: How Full-Stack Codesign Solves AI’s Memory Challenge
items.d: Larger models, longer contexts and agentic applications are increasing GPU memory pressure while supply tightens and prices rise — a trend expected to continue through the near term. NVIDIA works closely with memory partners to rapidly…
items.x:
Larger models, longer contexts and agentic applications are increasing GPU memory pressure while supply tightens and prices rise — a trend expected to continue through the near term.
NVIDIA works closely with memory partners to rapidly adopt the latest memory technologies. NVIDIA was first to adopt HBM3e and HBM4 technologies into an accelerated computing stack.
But the approach isn’t to simply pack more memory onto the GPU. It’s full-stack codesign. NVIDIA intentionally designs GPUs, CPUs, networking, storage and software together to get more useful work out of memory at every layer of the AI factory.
That matters because an AI factory runs on a memory and storage hierarchy. GPU high-bandwidth memory (HBM) is the fastest, most expensive and most contested tier — with model weights and KV cache competing for limited capacity. Below it sit CPU memory, local SSDs and shared storage, each trading speed for more capacity at a lower cost per bit.
How much useful work a byte does depends on how well the whole hierarchy is used: shrinking what must be stored, placing it on the right tier and bringing it back to the GPU before it’s needed.
Byte for byte, NVIDIA makes the most efficient use of memory at every layer — and the results show it.

وتشمل القدرات التي أعلنتها كراودسترايك اكتشاف وكلاء الذكاء الاصطناعي ومراقبة سلوكهم والأنظمة والبيانات التي يصلون إليها، إلى جانب إيقاف الأنشطة الخبيثة المرتبطة بهم في الوقت الفعلي. كما تعتمد المنصة، بحسب الشركة، على قدرات الكشف المدعومة بالذكاء الاصطناعي ومعلومات التهديدات العالمية وخدمات صيد التهديدات التي يقدمها خبراؤها.
وذكرت الشركة أن بنية الخدمة صُممت للتوافق مع متطلبات الأمن السيبراني والسحابة وحماية البيانات ذات الصلة في السعودية.

items.t: You can post AI music straight to SoundCloud from ElevenLabs
items.d: After partnering with Moises earlier this year, SoundCloud is now adding integration with another AI music platform, ElevenLabs. Now, rather than having to export and download your outputs from ElevenLabs and then upload them to…
items.x:
SoundCloud is partnering with another generative AI music service, ElevenLabs.
The integration between SoundCloud and ElevenLabs isn’t as deep as the Moises integration. That lets users pull tracks from SoundCloud into Moises for stem separation and remixing, then republish them directly to SoundCloud.
In general, SoundCloud has seemed more willing to embrace AI-generated music than other streaming services. While it “encourages” users subject to EU rules to label tracks as “AI-generated or manipulated” and has rules against impersonation, it’s also partnered with multiple generative AI music platforms. SoundCloud has also avoided the loud-and-proud press releases detailing how many spammy AI songs it’s removed from its platform, or bragging about demonetizing them.

items.t: Aina’s smart ring has a screen, a joystick, and a mic so you can talk to AI agents
items.d: Aina's ring can also take calls and help you dictate notes on your Mac.
items.x:
Aina's ring can also take calls and help you dictate notes on your Mac.
Hardware startup Aina released a smart ring today that features a screen, a joystick, and a mic so that you can talk to your agents and take notes. The $399 ring has a speaker so you can take calls using it as well.
The startup, which raised $5.5 million in July, is positioning the ring as a controller of sorts for both AI and non-AI apps.
The company previously made Mirage, a three-key controller that let you invoke buttons based on the app on your Mac’s screen. For instance, if you were on a Google Meet call, you could map keys to camera on/off, mic mute/unmute, or to leave the meeting.
Aina has baked in lessons from that device to create the new ring, which it’s simply calling “AI ring.” Using its mic, you can take notes, send a prompt to agents, set reminders, and dictate notes on your Mac using Wispr Flow or the startup’s own dictation engine.
Now, there are already smart rings in the market that do similar things, like the Pebble Index 01, Sandbar Stream, Oasis, and Natura, which is probably why Aina has added more controls and functionality to stand out.

items.t: The hidden supply chain costs of the AI boom
items.d: Today, I’m talking with Willy Shih, an economist, a professor of management practice at Harvard Business School, and the author of the upcoming book, Where Does My Stuff Come From? The Powerful Economics Behind Global Supply Chains. Willy…
items.x:
Today, I’m talking with Willy Shih, an economist, a professor of management practice at Harvard Business School, and the author of the upcoming book, Where Does My Stuff Come From? The Powerful Economics Behind Global Supply Chains .
Willy is one of my all-time favorite Decoder guests — his way of looking at the world through our supply chains is just a fascinating way of making sense of the global economy. I first met Willy in 2019, while The Verge was covering Foxconn’s promise to build an LCD fab in Wisconsin. That obviously never happened, but Willy called it right away because he could see the supply chain to support a fab simply wasn’t in place. We also had Willy on the show in 2021 to talk about what was then the pandemic-era chip shortage.
Now, five years later, we’re in another manufacturing mess, as we stand in the middle of a political fight over whether globalization is coming to an end. Trumps’ tariffs keep changing, the factories that were supposed to reshore in America mostly haven’t materialized, and AI is devouring the planet’s computing resources during an unprecedented infrastructure buildout.
Willy’s new book is all about the economics underlying these complex systems, which our politicians and regulators seem to insistently ignore.

items.t: Box taps Nvidia’s Nemotron for new agent-first content retrieval system
items.d: The system can supposedly answer queries four times faster, with 20% fewer errors and 90% fewer tokens used.
items.x:
The system can answer queries four times faster, with 20% fewer errors and 90% fewer tokens used.
At its developer conference on Thursday, Box showed off a new feature that will build Nvidia’s Nemotron embedding system into the core of its product.
Called Box Content Retrieval, the new feature allows agents to answer queries far more effectively by relying on the embedded metadata created by Nemotron.
Box says the upshot for users is faster, more accurate and less expensive queries. Nvidia’s VP of generative AI software, Kari Briski, told TechCrunch that she expects queries to be answered four times faster, with 20% fewer errors and 90% fewer tokens used.
The system will be available to all of Box’s Enterprise Advance customers, rolling out early next year.
“This dramatically boosts both the relevance of our search technology for agents,” Box CEO Aaron Levie said. “Instead of an agent having to kind of read through each document, we can send back chunks from the documents that are most relevant to the user’s query or whatever the the task is that the agent is doing.”
The feature is an implementation of Nvidia’s Nemotron Embed project, which offers open-weight embedding models to improve automated retrieval systems.

items.t: A YC startup is putting $1M behind 5 unsolved materials science problems for AI
items.d: While frontier AI models have solved a remarkable series of outstanding mathematics problems and made progress in the life sciences, they have yet to truly plumb the complex physics in advanced materials.
items.x:
Discovered Materials, a months-old YC startup that uses AI to find chip materials, is offering $200,000 for each solution to five open materials science problems.
Discovered Materials, a months-old, San Francisco startup using AI models to find new substances for building advanced chips, announced a million-dollar challenge for AI models to solve five critical problems in materials science.
While frontier AI models have solved a remarkable series of outstanding mathematics problems and made progress in the life sciences, they have yet to truly plumb the complex physics in advanced materials.
“It’s more difficult to specify problems clearly in materials science because it’s not like math, where you have a very specific definition and can get to a yes or no,” said Advaith Sridhar, a co-founder of Discovered Materials, which was part of Y Combinator’s spring 2026 batch. “We came to this discussion [wondering], what are the grand challenges in this field? How do we know AI is making progress?”
Though materials science doesn’t have an equivalent of the Millennium Prize Problems, Discovered Materials recruited an advisory group of academics at leading global universities to spell out five open problems.

items.t: Agility Robotics' Nasdaq debut invites scrutiny of humanoid robot market
items.d: US leader in deploying humanoid robots goes public on the Nasdaq stock exchange.
items.x:
Humanoid robots remain unproven at scale and have not yet achieved widespread commercialization, compared with industrial robots that have decades of proven track records in warehouses and factories. That frank acknowledgment is among the risks outlined in a securities filing by Agility Robotics—the first dedicated developer of humanoid robots to become a publicly traded company in the United States.
The robotics company headquartered in Salem, Oregon, previously became the first to achieve full-time commercial deployment of humanoid robots at a customer warehouse in 2024. Now, Agility’s public listing on the Nasdaq stock exchange as of November 5 has come with financial disclosures detailing how the company plans to build a business around renting out or selling humanoid robots to perform manual labor.
“When we are doing robots as a service, it is much lower risk for customers to use it because they are getting a return on investment on day one,” Jonathan Hurst , co-founder and chief robot officer at Agility Robotics, told Ars. “Because they're paying a rate that is comparable to the human labor rate, and that makes the economics pretty straightforward.”

items.t: Agility is the first pure humanoid robot company on the stock market. Are you buying?
items.d: Agility arrives on the Nasdaq today as the first publicly traded pure-play humanoid robotics company.
items.x:
Agility arrives on the Nasdaq today as the first publicly-traded pure-play humanoid robotics company.
Almost a year ago to the day, Figure AI CEO Colby Adcock responded to some gentle social media taunting from rival robotics company Agility with a prediction: “You’ll be bankrupt in <12 months.”
Instead, Agility is going public through a reverse-merger that will see it become a publicly-traded company and raise $465 million in new capital from retail investors and a tranche of private funding. The transaction will take place through a special purpose acquisition company, or SPAC.
“You don’t see a lot of dancing robots or backflipping robots from Agility,” CEO Peggy Johnson told TechCrunch ahead of the company’s market debut. “We stuck to our strategy, which [are] these manual, very repetitive jobs, that it’s hard to find humans to do.”
Agility predates the recent boom in physical AI investment. The company was spun out of Oregon State University in 2015 by a group of researchers who made headway in figuring out how to get a robot to walk safely on two legs. The company has focused on deploying a handful of its Digit robots in industrial settings with nine different customers, including Schaeffler, GXO, Toyota Motor Manufacturing Canada, and Mercado Libre.

items.t: SuperCLUE Office Agent Benchmark Crowns Doubao Work Ahead of Kimi Work and WorkBuddy
items.d: SuperCLUE's October 2026 office-agent test scored Doubao Work 85.33 overall, with Kimi Work and Tencent WorkBuddy close behind across document, writing and data tasks.
items.x:
Chinese evaluation group SuperCLUE has released its October 2026 SuperCLUE-Office end-to-end office-agent benchmark, and ByteDance's Doubao Work took first place with an overall score of 85.33, according to results published on SuperCLUE's site and reported by IT Home. Moonshot AI's Kimi Work placed second at 84.57 and Tencent's WorkBuddy third at 83.99. The ranking is a vendor benchmark from SuperCLUE; Pandaily is reporting the organizer's scores, not an independent re-test.
SuperCLUE-Office focuses on whether office agents can finish real deliverables in Word, PowerPoint, Excel and charts. The October run covered three dimensions — document processing, materials drafting and data analysis — across 13 secondary tasks, and scored five capability areas: file and environment operations, multi-file planning, constraint following, content quality, and safety and permission boundaries. Eight Chinese office agents took part: Doubao Work, Kimi Work, WorkBuddy, Baidu Dazi, Alibaba's QwenWork, SenseTime's Raccoon Work, iFLYTEK Spark Work and 360's Nano Work.
The top four finished within 2.65 points of one another. Baidu Dazi scored 82.68, QwenWork 78.38, Raccoon Work 69.20, iFLYTEK Spark Work 69.12 and Nano Work 53.13.

items.t: Alibaba Cloud Lingjun Zhenwu M890 SuperPoD Adds Day-Zero Support for Kimi K3.1 Pro
items.d: Alibaba Cloud says its Lingjun Zhenwu M890 SuperPoD now runs Moonshot AI's 2.8T Kimi K3.1 Pro on day zero via vLLM and SGLang, with Zhongwei invite testing and Panmai 920 NICs.
items.x:
Alibaba Cloud says its Lingjun Zhenwu M890 SuperPoD has completed day-zero adaptation for Moonshot AI's Kimi K3.1 Pro weights and finished full-stack validation on the vLLM and SGLang inference frameworks, IT Home reported on November 5, citing the cloud provider. The company also opened invite testing for a new SuperPoD region in Zhongwei, Ningxia, expanding the sites where large open-weight models can be hosted on its self-developed accelerators.
Kimi K3.1 Pro is a 2.8-trillion-parameter sparse mixture-of-experts model with about a one-million-token context window, hybrid Kimi Delta Attention and DSA sparse attention, and multi-token prediction. Those traits put heavy demands on memory capacity and high-speed scale-up interconnects. Alibaba Cloud, T-Head and the Kimi team said they jointly adapted the model on the T-Head SAIL software stack, with work on FlashMLA, DeepGEMM MoE operators, MegaMoE and MoonEP so customers can deploy inference on bare-metal SuperPoD instances or through the REIN intelligent engine service.

items.t: Moonshot AI Launches Kimi Hosted Agents as a Managed Agent-Harness Cloud Service
items.d: Moonshot AI's Kimi Hosted Agents offers a 24/7 managed agent harness with sandboxes, audit trails, Inference Hook and eight finance templates, so teams need not self-host the runtime.
items.x:
Moonshot AI has launched Kimi Hosted Agents, a cloud service that packages the agent runtime, or harness, as a managed product rather than leaving enterprises to build and maintain that layer themselves, according to IT Home and the company's open-platform documentation. The offering is framed as Harness as a Service: teams configure agents on Kimi's infrastructure and get a 24/7 hosted environment for long-running tasks and multi-agent collaboration.
Companies can point agents at internal systems for monitoring, research and operations work, or embed them in customer-facing products as research or support assistants. Kimi Hosted Agents provides isolated sandboxes with network-access controls, session boundaries that operators can stop at any time, and execution logs that can be exported for audit. Usage reports break out sandbox hours, model inference and plugin calls; IT Home cites a sandbox rate of 0.072 yuan per hour plus model and plugin charges.
The platform currently lists more than 140 skills and more than 30 plugins covering web search, professional data queries, office documents and content generation. Developers can also attach their own tools, data sources and MCP services.

items.t: Baidu Tests a New Way to Train Robotaxis
items.d: SHENZHEN, China — Nov. 3: Baidu’s Apollo unit unveiled Apollo World, an agent-driven multimodal world model for physical AI, at its AI Day event in Shenzhen. Why it matters: Apollo defines a world model by two requirements: causality and…
items.x:
SHENZHEN, China — Nov. 3: Baidu’s Apollo unit unveiled Apollo World, an agent-driven multimodal world model for physical AI, at its AI Day event in Shenzhen.
The model is already being used to test and validate Apollo Go as the driverless ride-hailing service expands into more markets, according to the company.
Why it matters: Apollo defines a world model by two requirements: causality and interactivity — the future follows the past, and the world responds to the vehicle’s actions.
“A world model is not a painter that generates videos, but an examiner of autonomous-driving safety,” said Liang Wang, chief architect of Baidu’s Intelligent Driving Group.
What happened: Apollo World creates a closed-loop virtual environment where AI-driven cars and pedestrians react to the vehicle, while simulated camera and lidar data feed back into the AI driver.
It can test complete trips, not just isolated maneuvers.
“Apollo World focuses more on closed-loop simulation of complete tasks,” said Ze Yang, Baidu IDG distinguished architect and world-model lead.
Liang Wang, chief architect at Baidu’s Intelligent Driving Group (left) and Ze Yang, a Baidu IDG distinguished architect and world-model lead (right), introduced Apollo World.
The system aims to cut costly road testing.

items.t: Oracle reportedly cancels $7 billion Tencent AI chip lease under US pressure
items.d: Oracle has canceled a five-year agreement to lease advanced AI chips to Tencent after pressure from the Trump administration, the Financial Times reported on November 4. The deal, valued at approximately $7 billion, would have given…
items.x:
Oracle has canceled a five-year agreement to lease advanced AI chips to Tencent after pressure from the Trump administration, the Financial Times reported on November 4. The deal, valued at approximately $7 billion, would have given Tencent access to around 100,000 advanced AI chips across Oracle data centers in Southeast Asia.
US officials raised concerns about the arrangement with Oracle, according to the report. Tencent also received visits from senior officials in Guangdong who asked it to support Chinese chips. Reuters said it could not independently verify the report, and Oracle, Tencent and the White House did not respond to its requests for comment. [ Reuters ]

Nothing plans to launch its first AI-native hardware product in December, founder and CEO Carl Pei said on November 4. Pei described the forthcoming device as a productivity tool without a screen, adding that its functions could not have been delivered through an app alone.
In an essay titled “Toolmakers,” Pei argued that AI tools lack much of the context surrounding people’s work, including conversations and ideas that users do not manually enter into a chatbot. He suggested that everyday hardware could help close that gap. Nothing has not disclosed the device’s precise form, specifications or price. [ Gizbot ]

items.t: Moonshot AI releases Kimi K3.1 Pro model weights
items.d: Moonshot AI has released the weights of Kimi K3.1 Pro on Hugging Face, making its flagship multimodal model available for independent deployment. The model uses a mixture-of-experts architecture with 2.8 trillion total parameters and…
items.x:
Moonshot AI has released the weights of Kimi K3.1 Pro on Hugging Face, making its flagship multimodal model available for independent deployment. The model uses a mixture-of-experts architecture with 2.8 trillion total parameters and approximately 104 billion activated per inference, and supports a context window of around one million tokens.
K3.1 Pro builds on Kimi K3 with expanded reinforcement learning for coding, 3D creation, financial research and long-running agent tasks. The weights release follows the model’s earlier availability through Kimi’s applications and API. Huawei has also announced inference support through vLLM Ascend and SGLang, covering its Atlas A3 and Ascend 950 systems. [ Moonshot AI ]

items.t: China Merchants' LionRock AI Lab Open-Sources Lion-ER-35B-A3B Embodied Reasoning Model
items.d: China Merchants' LionRock AI Lab open-sourced Lion-ER-35B-A3B, a 3B-active embodied reasoning model built with a capability-driven data engine that beat its base on ten benchmarks.
items.x:
The LionRock AI Lab under the China Merchants Group Advanced Technology Research Institute has released Lion-ER-35B-A3B, an embodied reasoning vision-language model meant to help robots understand three-dimensional space, object states and task progress, QbitAI reported on November 4. The weights are available on Hugging Face under the Apache 2.0 license.
Lion-ER, short for LionRock Embodied Reasoner, is a mixture-of-experts model with about 35 billion total parameters and about 3 billion active per token. According to its model card, it is fine-tuned from Qwen3.6-35B-A3B. The lab says the model improved on its base across all ten public embodied and visual reasoning benchmarks it tested, reaching an equal-weight average of 65.29, with every score averaged over four sampled answers per question.
Among individual results, the lab reports a Where2Place spatial placement score of 64.28, up 9.30 points on the base model, and 64.38 on the ERQA embodied reasoning benchmark, up 6.19 points. It scored 89.33 on the SAT spatial reasoning benchmark, and the trajectory understanding subcategory of ERQA rose 12.12 points to 68.18.
The lab argues that more robot data does not automatically mean more capability.

items.t: openJiuwen's Hyper-Agent Swarm Puts Persistent AI Agents Into Work Chats as Digital Employees
items.d: openJiuwen's Hyper-Agent swarm architecture lets persistent agents with their own identities and inboxes join Feishu and DingTalk groups as digital employees via WorkSwarm.
items.x:
openJiuwen, the Huawei-backed open-source agent community, has released Hyper-Agent, a swarm architecture that moves agents out of single chat sessions and into real work group chats as persistent digital employees, according to a community release published by IT Home. The capabilities ship in openJiuwen WorkSwarm, whose code is open-sourced on GitHub as JiuwenSwarm.
The core change is how agents relate to sessions. Instead of an agent being tied to one conversation, a Persistent Agent keeps its own identity and state and takes on work continuously, while sessions become an underlying resource the system allocates, schedules concurrently and resumes with context. A gateway connects instant messaging apps and a web interface, and an AgentServer schedules agents and work sessions. The community says this builds on its earlier Persistent Session work and lets one agent follow several jobs across multiple third-party group chats.
In WorkSwarm, users create these agents in an employee center from expert templates or from scratch, setting duties, working style, delivery requirements, skills, connectors, knowledge sources and even a dedicated email inbox.

items.t: Moxin Technology Launches MoWorld 2.0, an Ascend-Native 4D World Model That Simulates Physics
items.d: Moxin Technology's MoWorld 2.0 adds gravity, elasticity and fluids to 4D Gaussian scenes, runs video inference at about 70 fps and is trained and deployed on Huawei Ascend.
items.x:
Moxin Technology unveiled MoWorld 2.0, a 4D world model trained and deployed natively on Huawei Ascend hardware, at a World Internet Conference forum in Wuzhen on November 4, IT Home reported. The release follows MoWorld 1.0 in July.
The company says the main step up is physics. MoWorld 2.0 folds gravity, elasticity, buoyancy, lighting and heat, along with the properties of rigid bodies, soft bodies, fluids and deformable materials, into how it builds and interacts with spaces. Its output is 4D Gaussian assets that can be used for simulation, rendered in real time and reused repeatedly.
Because it models several physical factors, Moxin says the model generates not only the appearance of a space and its objects but also reasons in real time about how objects interact, how external forces act on them and how the environment changes. One demonstration shows a breeze turning the pages of a book and a bookmark falling to the floor, which requires accounting for wind strength and direction, the flexibility of paper, the weight of the bookmark and the rigidity of the floor. Other demos show scenes that can be edited and interacted with, and time that can be sped up or slowed down.
MoWorld 2.0 was trained and deployed on a fully domestic Ascend computing base.

items.t: Huawei's Xiaoyi Work Is First to Run openPangu-2.1-Pro, Billed for HarmonyOS Task Enhancement
items.d: IT Home found openPangu-2.1-Pro live first in Huawei's Xiaoyi Work agent, labeled HarmonyOS task enhancement, days after openPangu-2.0 was slated to leave Huawei Cloud MaaS.
items.x:
Huawei's AI work agent Xiaoyi Work has become the first product to offer openPangu-2.1-Pro, a new version of the company's open Pangu model family, IT Home found in hands-on testing reported on November 5. In the app, the model is labeled as offering HarmonyOS task enhancement.
The appearance comes days after Huawei Cloud said on November 1 that its MaaS model-as-a-service platform will stop selling openPangu-2.0-Flash and openPangu-2.0-Pro on November 6 and take both offline at midnight on November 30. Huawei said at the time that new openPangu models were being planned and would be rolled out over time.
Huawei has not published details of openPangu-2.1-Pro. No public information is available on its parameter count, active parameters, context length or training data, and the model has not been formally released. IT Home concluded that it is a very new model currently available only inside Xiaoyi Work. For reference, the openPangu-2.0-Pro model it succeeds was opened earlier this year with 505 billion total parameters, 180 billion sparsely activated parameters and a 512K context window, trained entirely on Ascend NPUs.
Xiaoyi Work is positioned as an AI assistant for office work, coding and creative tasks across HarmonyOS phones, tablets and PCs, with a Windows client as well.

items.t: Huawei Ascend Adds Day-Zero Support for Kimi K3.1 Pro Across Atlas A3 and Ascend 950 SuperPoDs

Using vLLM Ascend and SGLang, developers can deploy the model on Atlas 800 A3 servers, the Atlas 900 A3 SuperPoD and the Ascend 950 SuperPoD series from the day of release.
Kimi K3.1 Pro is the first model in Moonshot AI's K3.1 series. It is a mixture-of-experts model with native visual understanding and a context window of about one million tokens, activating roughly 104 billion parameters per inference step. It keeps K3's hybrid linear attention built on Kimi Delta Attention (KDA) layers and adds DSA sparse attention layers in place of some full-attention layers to cut the cost of long-context modeling.
That architecture is where most of the adaptation work went. Huawei said its inference team built on its earlier Kimi K3 adaptation, analyzing the new model in advance and working on model integration, operator development and service validation in parallel.

Apple is cutting the daily amount its engineering teams can spend on AI, Bloomberg reported Wednesday. It’s a big change for a company that has worked to integrate the technology into its engineering processes.
In October, Apple lowered the daily AI spending cap for its engineering teams, decreasing it from $300 to $200, the outlet reported. And more cuts are in the works, with some allowances falling to $100 a day, sources tell Bloomberg. Outside engineering, Apple is reportedly weighing a daily limit as low as $25 a day.

items.t: After the midterms, a bigger clash over data centers could be coming
items.d: Data center opposition crossed party lines in Tuesday’s midterms.

Data center opposition crossed party lines in Tuesday’s midterms.
The November 3 midterm results gave Democrats full control of Congress, setting the stage for what could be one of the most divided U.S. governments this decade, with Republicans in the White House.
Tuesday’s results suggest that anger over data centers, the large facilities that house the computers powering AI, is becoming a political force. With Democrats now in control of Congress, that could lead to new limits on where data centers can be built and how much say local communities have.
Data centers became a ballot-box issue in various states. An NBC exit poll showed how concerned voters are about AI: More than half of respondents believe that AI will do more harm than good, while almost 80% are against the building of data centers in their neighborhoods. Almost 60%, meanwhile, said data centers were a crucial or major factor in their vote. Nadine Smith, president and CEO of the racial justice organization Color of Change, called Tuesday’s election a referendum on “who this economy is built for.”
“National security matters,” Smith said, referring to a common argument from data center supporters that the infrastructure is essential for the U.S. to stay ahead in war and in its rivalry with China.

items.t: A Closer Look at Phonon TTS. Launching High-Quality On-Device Speech That Tops the Benchmarks.
items.x:
We’re on a journey to advance and democratize artificial intelligence through open source and open science.
Two weeks ago, we opened up Phonon, our small text-to-speech model that runs on your own device. It needs no server and no network, and what you type stays with you.
We've been very happy with the reception so far. So here's the story of the launch: why we built Phonon, what it can do, the demos that came with it, and how it did on Hugging Face's Open TTS Leaderboard.
Most voice AI lives in the cloud: every sentence makes a round trip to a server. Phonon runs on your own device instead. Your text stays there and the voice works without a network. We’ve also opened the weights. Phonon 31m is Apache 2.0, so you can use it for free, even in a commercial product. The other models are CC BY-NC, so they’re free for non-commercial projects. If you’re building something commercial with those, pricing is based on your number of users, not how much speech you generate.
Getting a good voice to run on a small device has always been hard. You could make the model small, but then it didn’t sound great. Or you could make it sound great, but then it wouldn’t fit. We addressed both.
We announced Phonon in April and spent the next six months building on it with partners and early users.

items.t: AI for scientific discovery: How researchers use Claude
items.d: We analyzed 207,000 research sessions to learn how Claude is used in science, why some tasks get more use than others, and how AI could speed up discovery.
items.x:
In this report, we use privacy-preserving infrastructure to study the scientific use of Claude, Claude Code, and Claude Science. We document how usage varies across scientific fields and research tasks, identify what explains these usage patterns, and outline scenarios for how AI could accelerate research.
Johannes Hermle*, Ben Jones*, Lukas Althoff*, Ryan Heller, Thomas Lyttelton, Carolyn Stein, Nathan Wilmers, Maxim Massenkoff, Peter McCrory
Science has been described as an “endless frontier” (Bush 1945). But how fast we explore that frontier has historically been limited by a scarce resource: the time and talent of human researchers. Artificial intelligence could ease that limit by amplifying what researchers can do, transforming both the process of discovery and the pace of exploration (Wang et al. 2023; Amodei 2024). Few applications of AI could matter more for human welfare. Given the highly cognitive nature of research compared with most sectors of the economy, AI’s effects may be particularly large and early in this domain.
Recent examples show AI playing a growing role in scientific discovery. In structural biology, AlphaFold predicted the three-dimensional shapes of over 200 million proteins (Jumper et al. 2021; Varadi et al.

items.t: AI PACs spent millions trying to shape Congress — here’s how they fared

AI industry PACs spent millions influencing the 2026 midterms, with mixed results. Political groups are already looking toward the next election cycle.
Political groups both supporting and opposing the AI industry spent millions of dollars trying to influence Tuesday’s midterm elections and shape the future of AI regulation. That spending produced mixed results, with some of the most heavily backed candidates losing their races.
On the industry side, two AI-focused political action committees (PACs) that raised and spent money to influence the elections — American Mission and Building the Future — collectively spent $4.8 million to back South Carolina Senate candidate Darlene Graham, who lost. American Mission is the Republican spending arm of Leading the Future (LTF), a broader political group backed by OpenAI President Greg Brockman and the VC firm Andreessen Horowitz.
American Mission also spent more than $500,000 apiece supporting Republican House candidates Aaron Flint in Montana and Laurie Buckhout in North Carolina, both of whom lost. LTF’s Democratic spending arm, Think Big, had better luck backing Florida Rep. Jared Moskowitz, who won reelection.
Groups advocating for stronger AI safeguards also saw mixed results.

While more people used an AI agent to order food through its delivery service, Uber Eats, the volume was still fairly small compared to the overall number of trips.
Uber’s chief financial officer, Balaji Krishnamurthy, told Wall Street analysts on the call that the company handled around 320 million trips and orders across Uber and Uber Eats during the week of Halloween, but only 500 Uber Eats orders were placed by an AI agent.
“It is very, very early and very limited traction that we are seeing so far,” said CEO Dara Khosrowshahi, referring to the low number of orders placed by AI agents. “Listen, we hope that there will be more traction.”
The surprisingly low numbers of AI-initiated transactions come amid growing hype for a new wave of AI agents that don’t just answer questions but also handle tasks on users’ behalf.

OpenAI’s chief global affairs officer Chris Lehane thinks the 2028 presidential election could be a defining moment for AI. And he wants politicians to start developing policies that address Americans’ concerns about the technology, rather than simply paying lip service to anti-AI sentiment and the backlash against data centers.
In a new essay, Lehane compares AI’s potential to reshape the economy to President Franklin D. Roosevelt’s New Deal, the 1930s set of federal programs and reforms enacted after industrialization and the Great Depression shattered the old economic order. He observes that Americans today feel similarly anxious about losing control over their economic futures and urges politicians to find a “compelling third path” that allows people to share in AI’s benefits. items.t: Dharma Field Extractor: Any Document In, Structured Fields in JSON Out
items.x:
A 2-billion-parameter model that extracts exactly the fields you ask for, from any document type, outperforming every frontier LLM we tested, at a fraction of the cost.
In April, we released DharmaOCR-LITE, a model specialized for OCR across a wide range of documents, from contracts and court filings to invoices, IDs and forms. The paper behind it made a narrow, well-measured case for domain specialization: a smaller model trained closer to its task beating general-purpose frontier APIs on that task.
OCR gives you the text on a page, faithful to the original formatting. That's exactly what you want when the job is the whole document, like a contract you'll read end to end or a manuscript you're digitizing.
However, there's a different use case: you don't want the page, you want specific fields out of it, in a shape a system downstream can consume. Every line item on an invoice, as a list. The patient name, exam type and date from a medical requisition, ready to schedule. The fields off an ID, mapped to the columns of an employee record.
Run that document through OCR and you get back everything printed on it, line by line, with no indication of which string is the exam type, which is the date or which number is the total.

items.t: Securing the agentic enterprise with data lineage
items.d: A sales representative asks an AI agent for customer pricing, and the agent pulls data from multiple sources: restricted pricing systems, internal communications, and archived quotes. The output looks accurate to the agent, so a second…
items.x:
A sales representative asks an AI agent for customer pricing, and the agent pulls data from multiple sources: restricted pricing systems, internal communications, and archived quotes. The output looks accurate to the agent, so a second agent uses the data to draft the proposal for the sales rep. No human checks either handoff. When it’s discovered that the proposal includes unapproved, confidential, and sensitive information, no one can trace where the problematic data entered the workflow or how it spread across systems, files, and agents.
This scenario illustrates why AI governance needs to evolve, rapidly and dynamically. As more enterprises begin to use agentic AI in daily workflows, they’re realizing that they must manage more than static files; they must manage moving and fragmented data that is continuously ingested, copied, summarized, transformed, reused, and redistributed in new forms. In short, AI security isn’t a tool problem; it’s a data visibility problem.
Consequently, traditional security approaches built solely around applications, systems, networks, or endpoints are no longer sufficient. Securing agentic AI at scale requires understanding how data moves.

The company said Hy4 can interpret charts and documents, reason across multiple images, and operate command-line tools and graphical interfaces. Targeted training covers applications such as Blender and CAD software, alongside tasks spanning multiple programs.

Standard API pricing remains unchanged from Hy4 preview at $0.834 per million input tokens and $2.501 per million output tokens, with a 50% discount on Tencent Cloud TokenHub through December 31.

items.x:
Even if employees pay for Claude or Codex out of their own pockets, they may no longer be able to use these tools freely to work with company code and internal documents.
According to recent reports , ByteDance has been tightening access to external AI tools across the company since the beginning of this month. The new rules primarily restrict employees from using personally purchased accounts for third-party AI tools such as Claude and Codex to access internal resources.
The restrictions cover all L4-level code repositories and Feishu documents across the company. Some use cases within the Seed team are reportedly exempt from the restrictions.
The notice was circulated internally and quickly sparked discussions among employees. Their concerns largely revolve around three questions: Will restrictions on external AI tools affect everyday development efficiency? Where exactly does the company’s data security boundary lie? And can ByteDance’s in-house AI tools meet developers’ needs?
In response, Hong Dingkun , ByteDance’s vice president of technology, addressed the concerns on the company’s internal platform.

items.t: DeepBlue Technology and Huawei Launch Wowoker, a HarmonyOS Work Phone Run by Sales Agents
items.d: DeepBlue Technology's Wowoker pairs Huawei Kirin hardware and HarmonyOS with sales agents that find leads, place AI calls and log every chat for employers.
items.x:
DeepBlue Technology launched Wowoker on October 29, an enterprise work phone developed with Huawei that the Shanghai-based AI company describes as the world's first large-model agent work phone, The Paper reported. IT Times followed up with details from the launch event.
According to DeepBlue, the device runs on Huawei Kirin chips, Huawei device hardware and HarmonyOS, combined with DeepBlue's multimodal large model, its Decision Model and its AgentOS agent orchestration system. Huawei provides the HarmonyOS ecosystem, hardware adaptation and enterprise security foundations, and offered 12 phone models for adaptation, so orders from teams of ten to groups buying hundreds of units can be matched to suitable hardware.
The phone is aimed squarely at sales teams rather than consumers. Its built-in agents handle customer acquisition, automated outbound calls and analysis of customer intent. A lead-generation agent takes a manager's industry and keyword settings, then searches Xiaohongshu, WeChat and Douyin for potential customers and starts conversations. DeepBlue said that in a test by an early customer, Greenland's OPC community, the agent screened more than 200 potential leads in half a day, with over 50 leading to meaningful exchanges.

items.t: HongYun's HyperLM V2.5 Adds Native Support for Huawei Ascend 950DT and Atlas 850E SuperPoD
items.d: HongYun's HyperLM V2.5 adapts to Huawei's Ascend 950DT and Atlas 850E, adding UnifiedBus 2.0 support, mxFP4 tuning, vNPU slicing and prefill-decode split inference.
items.x:
Beijing-based AI software company HongYun has released HyperLM V2.5, a new version of its combined training and inference platform for large models, IT Home and ifeng Tech reported on November 3. The company says it is the first to complete deep adaptation to Huawei's Ascend 950DT, is fully compatible with the air-cooled Atlas 850E SuperPoD and has passed Huawei's Ascend Native technical certification.
HongYun argues that adaptation is often defined too loosely, counting a model as supported once it installs and produces tokens. Its stated goal is to help government and enterprise customers running private deployments get more of the rated performance out of new accelerators. The company describes the Ascend 950DT as a flagship inference chip for bandwidth-heavy work such as large-scale chat, long documents and continuous agent reasoning, and says the air-cooled Atlas 850E fits existing data centers without facility retrofits.
HyperLM V2.5 adapts at several levels. At the interconnect level it supports Huawei's UnifiedBus 2.0, which the company says releases 13.4TB/s of system interconnect bandwidth so cross-card traffic does not bottleneck long contexts or prefill-decode disaggregation.

items.t: NetEase Yidun Unveils Agent Guard at Wuzhen to Police What AI Agents Do, Not Just What They Say
items.d: At Wuzhen, NetEase Yidun launched an AI security suite whose Agent Guard checks agent intent, permissions and tool calls, alongside Skill and MCP supply chain scans.
items.x:
NetEase Yidun, the content and risk-control security unit of NetEase's enterprise services business, launched what it calls an AI-native security product system at the 2026 World Internet Conference Light of Internet Expo in Wuzhen on November 3, Sina Tech and IT Home reported. The company's argument is that security has to move from controlling what AI says to controlling what AI does, as agents gain access to knowledge bases, business tools and enterprise systems.
Zhu Haoqi, vice general manager of NetEase's enterprise services business and head of Yidun, presented a two-way framework: using AI to strengthen security work, and using security tools to keep AI running within defined limits. He said risks now include AI-generated content, deepfakes, automated fraud, model jailbreaks, sensitive data leaks and agents executing actions beyond their permissions.
The product system has three layers. The first covers AI content and data security, including AI content moderation and analysis and a moderation agent called CMA. The second covers interaction and identity security, including business risk control, device fingerprinting, behavioral CAPTCHA and DeepGuard face anti-spoofing.

items.t: Huawei's openJiuwen Gives Agents Event-Based Video Memory, Cutting Answer Times by up to 97%
items.d: openJiuwen's OmniMem-Lens splits long videos at real event boundaries using sight and sound, lifting recall up to 45.7% and cutting agent answer times by up to 97%.
items.x:
openJiuwen, the Huawei-backed open-source agent framework, has released OmniMem-Lens, a multimodal memory capability in version 0.2.0 of its AgentMemory module that lets AI agents remember long videos by real events rather than fixed time slices, QbitAI reported on November 4.
The team argues that the common approach, cutting long videos into one-minute windows and storing each separately, breaks agent memory in two ways. A continuous scene split across windows leaves the agent with half the evidence, which invites hallucination. A few seconds of key action bundled with minutes of irrelevant footage gets buried in noise, lowering retrieval accuracy. Most event segmentation methods also rely on a single modality, so they miss topic changes when the picture stays still or scene changes when nobody speaks.
OmniMem-Lens tracks both streams. A visual track flags scene changes, while an audio track uses speech recognition to detect when a speaker switches topic even though the screen has not changed. Cross-checking the two places cuts at real event boundaries.

items.t: GPUWorks Open-Sources 40MB Inference Platform Running Ascend, PPU, Hygon and NVIDIA in One Cluster
items.d: Open-sourced under Apache-2.0, GPUWorks pools Ascend, T-Head PPU, Hygon and NVIDIA GPUs in one cluster; its developers say one server ran 1,003 GPU machines.
items.x:
GPUWorks, a lightweight enterprise AI inference platform, was open-sourced under the Apache-2.0 license on November 4, according to a release published by IT Home. The code is hosted on GitHub under the FlitAI organization, and enterprises and developers can use and modify it or contribute inference templates and chip adaptations.
The platform pulls accelerators from different vendors and sources into one managed pool, matches models to hardware, estimates GPU memory needs and deploys models from templates, then serves them through an OpenAI-compatible API. Supported chips include NVIDIA and AMD as well as Huawei Ascend, T-Head PPU and Hygon DCU. Bare-metal servers, virtual machines and cloud containers in company data centers, private clouds and public clouds can sit in the same cluster.
The developers emphasize its size. The installer is just over 40MB, installs with one command in about 60 seconds and does not require Kubernetes. Intranet users can import the installer, model files and runtime images offline. The catalog ships more than 1,000 launch configurations for nearly 400 models, bundling the image, inference engine, weight version and launch flags for each model and chip combination.

items.t: Midterm elections 2026: all the news
items.d: The 2026 midterm elections will determine the scope of President Donald Trump’s power in his final two years in office, and signal what voters care about going into the 2028 presidential election. While this year’s races are expected to be…
items.x:
The 2026 midterm elections will determine the scope of President Donald Trump’s power in his final two years in office, and signal what voters care about going into the 2028 presidential election. While this year’s races are expected to be most broadly defined by affordability issues, there’s several topics impacting the tech industry that appear to be on voters’ minds.
Among them are concerns about data centers, and whether voters will have to bear the burden of higher energy costs, AI safety, and the rapid expansion of surveillance technology through Flock. There’s also the question of how to tax billionaires’ wealth in California, a topic that has driven heavy tech spending and creative stock class structures meant to keep tech executives from fleeing the state should a ballot measure pass.
The next Congress is likely to continue grappling with how to regulate AI, and stem the data center backlash, among other issues.

items.t: Lenovo Kaitian Unveils AI Host With Zhaoxin KX-7000 CPU and Houmo LQ50 NPU for Local 35B Models
items.d: Lenovo Kaitian's 1.6L AI host pairs a Zhaoxin KX-7000 with a Houmo LQ50 NPU for 160 TOPS, running Qwen3.6-35B-A3B locally at about 29 tokens per second.
items.x:
Lenovo's Kaitian line has launched its first AI host built for China's Xinchuang (IT application innovation) market, a 1.6-liter desktop that pairs a Zhaoxin CPU with a Houmo AI NPU to run models of around 35 billion parameters locally, according to IT Home and a company article carried by Jiemian.
The machine uses an eight-core Zhaoxin KX-7000 processor and a Houmo Liqing LQ50 NPU. The shipping configuration delivers 160 TOPS of INT8 compute, with an NPU option of up to 320 TOPS. The NPU has 24GB of dedicated memory with 153.6GB/s of bandwidth. The host runs Kylin OS and comes preloaded with Lenovo's Tianxi AI Pro agent software.
Lenovo said it has tested the device with open-source models including the Qwen3.5 series and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B. With the 24GB NPU and W4A8 quantization, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B generated text at about 28.99 tokens per second in local inference, and the system supports inputs of up to 200,000 tokens for long documents and multi-turn tasks. Houmo's software platform provides quantization, compilation, runtime management and profiling tools for developers porting models.
The company pitches the host as an always-on digital employee.

items.x:
SenseTime has released the official version of SenseNova 6.8 Flash, a model update focused on office collaboration and design generation, according to a November 2 post on the company's Chinese website. The model adds long-term memory and cross-session task collaboration, and extends generation to animated slides, animated posters, web pages, SVG graphics and Blender 3D scenes.
SenseTime describes the office features as a shift toward proactive assistance. Using long-term memory, the model tracks a user's goals and constraints and, when relevant information changes, flags affected items and suggests adjustments. In one demo, built on an internal build of SenseTime's Raccoon office agent, the model links a new product feature to a client who had earlier declined a deal for lack of private deployment and recommends following up. Another demo shows it compiling a departing employee's client history for a successor from authorized work records.
On design, SenseTime says the model treats narrative pacing as part of slide generation, planning what each page must convey before choreographing transitions, element entry order and chart animations within the final PPTX. Animated posters coordinate visual motion with text hierarchy.

items.t: Investigating vault particles with Claude
items.d: We’re sharing another finding from Anthropic’s biology research lab: the first 3D structure of a vault particle found in prokaryotic cells. Here, we describe how Claude helped at each step of this research.
items.x:
We’re sharing another finding from Anthropic’s biology research lab: the first 3D structure of a vault particle found in prokaryotic cells.
Biological cells were first detected in 1665, but more than three and a half centuries later, much of how they work remains unknown. Until relatively recently, the existence of some crucial components, let alone their function, was controversial. Even today, more than a third of the roughly 4,400 genes in one of the most comprehensively studied cells, the bacterium E. coli, remain poorly understood. Another such enigma is the vault particle.
A vault particle is a large, hollow protein shell found in nearly all the cells in our body. It was discovered in 1986 by Leonard Rome and Nancy Kedersha, but its function remains elusive. At roughly three times the mass of a ribosome, it’s one of the largest known molecular complexes in eukaryotes—organisms with complex cells, such as mammals (as opposed to simple, usually single-celled “prokaryotes,” such as bacteria). Vaults take their name from their shape. When observed under an electron microscope, the ribbed shell reminded Dr. Rome and Dr. Kedersha of the vaulted ceiling of a cathedral.

items.t: Anthropic is working on a system to prove AI models’ identity
items.d: Called FlashProve, the system would let anyone check that an AI response really came from the model it claims to be from.
items.x:
Called FlashProve, the system would let anyone check that an AI response really came from the model it claims to be from.
Anthropic is working on an open-source system to verify which AI model produced a given output, according to a blog post published Tuesday. The system, called FlashProve, is built to provide what researchers call “provable inference” – a cryptographic proof, essentially a mathematical guarantee, that a given output came from a specific model. It’s meant to let users confirm that the answer they received really came from the model they think they’re using.
Similar to cryptographic email signatures that let recipients confirm a message really came from its claimed sender, FlashProve would be robust against impostors attempting to disguise one model as another, even when the impostor is the lab that built and runs the model. In particular, the researchers note that the system could be used to prevent an AI company from secretly swapping in a cheaper model to cut costs, or a more expensive model to inflate its performance results.
FlashProve could also be used to verify claims by third parties that a specific task was done by an advanced model.
