items.t: Data centers are turning to old jet engines as the wait for power grows
items.d: The years-long wait for access to the grid and new turbines is causing data center builders to turn to an unusual, less-efficient and less environmentally friendly solution: once-discarded jet engines.
items.x:
The years-long wait for access to the grid and new turbines is causing data center builders to turn to an unusual, less efficient and less environmentally friendly solution: once-discarded jet engines.
Stuck in years-long lines for grid connections and new turbines, some AI data centers are making their own electricity with converted jet engines, the New York Times reported Tuesday.
The engines, pulled from retired aircraft and rebuilt to burn natural gas, aren’t anyone’s idea of a permanent power plant. But they’re another sign of how far power supply has fallen behind the AI buildout.
For companies stuck in those lines, the main draw of converted jet engines is how quickly the engines can be up and running. “It’s all about getting power as fast as possible,” Rystad Energy analyst Audun Martinsen told the Times. With jet-powered units, “they can have a data center running in 24 months,” he said.
Hooking up 100 megawatts to the grid in Northern Virginia, by comparison, takes about seven years, according to the International Energy Agency.

Ballistic Ventures, the cybersecurity-focused venture capital firm co-founded by former Kleiner Perkins partner Ted Schlein (pictured above, second from the right), is seeking to raise $490 million across two new funds, TechCrunch has learned through regulatory filings.
The San Francisco-based VC firm filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission this week to raise $360 million for its third flagship fund, matching the size of its previous fund raised in 2024, and another $130 million for a separate vehicle called Ballistic Ventures Fund B. Neither fund had recorded any sales at the time of filing.
The fundraising plans come as the growing use of artificial intelligence has raised concerns about more sophisticated cyberattacks. The rise of AI agents has also created new opportunities for cybersecurity startups and the venture capital firms backing them.
Founded in late 2021, Ballistic Ventures’ founding team includes Schlein, former AT&T Cybersecurity president Barmak Meftah and Roger Thornton, who co-founded security companies Fortify Software and AlienVault.

items.t: Hiding inside Palantir’s skyrocketing quarter is a foreboding signal
items.d: Palantir's U.S. commercial revenue surpassed U.S. government revenue for the first time ever.
items.x:
Palantir delivered such a huge third-quarter earnings report on Monday that its press release even bragged that the numbers were "crushing consensus
Yet, retail investors were lukewarm on the company on Tuesday, with the stock trading slightly down. That’s because Palantir’s enterprise sales, its big growth area, showed signs of slowing.
First, the good news for the company’s investors. Revenue grew 96% year over year to $2.31 billion, the first time it has ever surpassed the $2 billion mark. Palantir’s revenue, which also grew 20% from the previous quarter, beat analysts’ expectations of $2.18 billion. Palantir also reported adjusted earnings per share of $0.44 versus analysts’ expectations of $0.41. The company even upped its revenue guidance for the full year. Normally, that alone would send a stock soaring.
The clincher was that Palantir’s U.S. commercial revenue surpassed U.S. government revenue for the first time ever. The company reported $984 million in commercial contracts (up 148% from the year-ago quarter), versus $953 million in U.S. government revenue.
The reason for all this love from enterprises?

The company says the package is meant to help studios test gameplay ideas sooner, move engineering and art production forward, and bring player feedback from launch and live operations back into the next round of development.
In Kimi's description, the model reads design documents, screenshots, code and 3D assets and plans the work. Kimi Code handles implementation and changes inside a codebase, while Kimi Work takes on multi-step production tasks that span several files. Through plugins and tool calls, Kimi can operate on existing projects directly and hand back editable files along with a record of what it did. In Unity and Unreal Engine, once it has the project files and the necessary permissions, it first maps the code structure, scene hierarchy and module dependencies, makes the changes through editor plugins, and then checks the result against reproduction steps, logs and runtime data.

items.t: Ukraine’s drone strikes spur hasty Russian plans for underground data centers
items.d: Russia tries to fix exposed digital infrastructure as data center war backfires.
items.x:
Russian tech companies are scrambling to harden and hide their data centers underground after Ukrainian drone strikes damaged facilities housing AI supercomputers and disrupted cloud services for millions of Russian users. Meanwhile, the Kremlin is requiring data center owners to reserve computing capacity for emergency state needs and has even authorized possible use of foreign data centers.
These consequences of Russia's war against Ukraine come as the Russian military has bombarded Ukrainian cities with drones and missiles nearly night and day in recent months, along with specifically targeting Ukrainian data centers since late September. But Ukraine has retaliated with its own drone strikes on military and infrastructure targets across Russia, degrading or knocking out data centers operated by Russian tech giant Yandex , the state-owned bank Sberbank, social media site VKontakte, and the Russian Ministry of Finance.
Now, state-owned telecommunications company Rostelcom has raised the possibility of moving some Russian data centers underground in talks with the nickel and palladium mining company Norilsk, according to Russian newspaper Vedomosti .

While Google is trying to move beyond Chromebooks , the ubiquity of these devices has made the company's education products huge in schools. Now, Google says it will let educators choose whether to allow its AI tools in the classroom. However, blocking AI tools also means giving up search, leaving schools with a difficult decision.
Google's new overarching approach to AI in the classroom sounds good on the surface. After consulting educators, researchers, and lawmakers, Google has decided that schools using its education products will be opted out of AI tools by default. It will be up to administrators to manually enable them when these changes roll out in the coming months.
When you look at what Google considers to be an AI tool, the nature of the Faustian bargain becomes clear. The affected products are Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom, and Google Search . There's no picking and choosing—you either allow all the AI or none of it.

items.t: Qwen 3.8 27B on my laptop can interpret model weights, too
items.d: Article URL: https://simonwillison.net/2026/Nov/3/qwen-can-interpret-model-weights/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50355251 Points: 736 # Comments: 213
items.x:
Yesterday’s hot paper was Sparks of Weight-Space Programming: LLMs can natively read & write neural network weights by Rikiya Takehi, Jayden Teoh, Alex Zhang, and Omar Khattab. The paper found …
Here’s the highlight from their abstract, describing impressive capabilities for GPT-6 Astra and coining the term Weight-Space Programming for when LLMs analyze and modify model weights:
Just by looking at the raw weights, GPT-6 Astra can tell what a network was trained to do. And without any environment feedback, it has no trouble writing, from scratch, small game-playing networks that outplay networks trained with PPO for 100 million steps.
Likewise, asked to make Qwen3.5-0.8B better at math without gradients, Astra identifies an issue in its weights causing reasoning loops that Qwen’s own model card warns about, and fixes this by natively editing 0.016% of the weights. With the same sampling settings, this weight correction raises MATH-500 from 7.9% to 48.1% and generalizes out of the box to instruction following, raising IFEval by 3x.
All of this is possible without allowing Astra to write training loops. It uses its reasoning to figure out what each part of a neural network computes, or should compute, and changes the weights accordingly.

items.t: StateBench: Testing how language models track state changes over long documents
items.x:
We’re introducing StateBench, a benchmark for long-context state tracking—how well language models keep track of information about entities in long documents as they evolve.
State tracking underlies tasks from reading code, where variables are assigned and reassigned, to following a story as characters physically move around and objects change hands. For example, if a mystery novel states that “John gave Mary the knife” right before a murder occurs, it’s important to know that the state of each character has changed. However, not all state-tracking problems are created equal: some require only finding the latest update; harder ones require following a chain of changes, where one missed step can throw off the final answer. For example, a harder variant of our mystery state tracking would be if John gave Mary the item in his backpack, with it previously known that Edward put a knife in John’s backpack.
Transformers have well-documented theoretical limits on hard variants of state tracking with long dependency chains, helping motivate recurrent and hybrid architectures such as Gated DeltaNet that carry a running memory forward.

items.t: Anthropic is still grappling with the economics of compute
items.d: At a moment when Anthropic's compute margins should be getting better, they’re getting worse.
items.x:
At a moment when Anthropic's compute margins should be getting better, they’re getting worse.
There’s a lot of mystery around the finances of major AI labs, and as Anthropic inches towards its IPO, we’re starting to get some answers. In particular, the company is finally disclosing more about the economics of compute, and how much it of Anthropic’s skyrocketing revenue is being lost to compute costs.
In a new filing on Monday, Anthropic released data that showed those margins on compute actually getting worse. The filing was an update to the S-1 released last week — but where that filing’s financial disclosures only covered through June 30th of this year, the new data extended to disclose results through an extra quarter, to September 30th. Broadly, Anthropic had a good quarter: revenue reached $17 billion, up from $11.5 billion in the previous quarter, suggesting durable growth. But the operating loss grew at the same time, thanks in large part to growing compute costs.
Looking at the compute margins makes the picture even worse. In the new quarter, compute took up 58% of the company’s revenue, up from 48% the quarter before.

items.t: Agentic cheminformatics with Google Antigravity
items.d: Learn how Google Antigravity and our Cheminformatics Skills accelerate drug discovery workflows, search compounds, and propose novel rigidified macrocycles.
items.x:
Learn how Google Antigravity and our Cheminformatics Skills accelerate drug discovery workflows, search compounds, and propose novel rigidified macrocycles.
Zoi Tsangalidou, Ruijie (Kelly) Zhang, Sukhdeep Singh and Michael V. LeVine
Designing new medicines requires curating complex data from charts, figures and literature, training predictive models, and proposing candidate molecules to synthesize — a workflow that typically takes multiple days for a single iteration.
Here we show how Google Antigravity, equipped with our new Cheminformatics Skills, accelerates drug discovery workflows. Using real-world lung cancer treatments, an agent searches through thousands of compounds, performs matched molecular pair analysis, and proposes novel rigidified macrocycles with synthetic routes in just an hour.
Chemistry is one of science’s richest public records — spanning millions of structures across journal articles and vendor catalogs. It provides a common representation that links physics and mathematics to the life and environmental sciences.

items.t: Palette: teaching a small model to build decks in your design language
items.x:
Ask a frontier model for a slide deck and you'll get a good one. Ask for ten and they start to look alike: the same tasteful defaults, the same house style, a faint "AI-generated deck" look. That's fine until you want the deck to look like your template. Frontier models have their own house style, and no amount of prompting stops them drifting back to it. And sometimes the content is confidential and can't leave your systems at all.
Both of those point to a model you own: open weights, running on your own infrastructure, trained on your own design language. The catch is that small open models, the kind you'd actually self-host, are bad at this. Their decks come out broken: titles that vanish into the background, text running off the slide, shapes stacked on top of each other.
Palette tests one bet: that a small open-weight model, trained on synthetic data in your design language and checked by a harness, can compete with frontier systems while you keep ownership of the result. We fine-tuned a 20B model to build decks the way people do: a designer plans the deck and a coder draws each slide. Its training data follows the IBM Design Language, and on PresentBench it ranks first on two of the three domains we measured.

items.t: AI Is Changing How Semiconductor Fabs Work — and Engineers Are Moving Faster Because of It
items.d: Demand for advanced chips is rising. The processes to build them are getting more complex. And the margin for error is shrinking. For engineers, understanding how a process change will behave, how a material will interact with a new step…
items.x:
Demand for advanced chips is rising. The processes to build them are getting more complex. And the margin for error is shrinking.
For engineers, understanding how a process change will behave, how a material will interact with a new step, how a defect maps back to a root cause are critical, challenging steps in semiconductor manufacturing — and these analyses can take days. Physical experiments on a fab line are slow and expensive. A wrong call on yield or process quality has real consequences.
AI is transforming semiconductor manufacturing, impacting what engineers can do — and how fast.
Accelerated computing shortens simulation time, allowing engineers to evaluate more alternatives before committing to physical trials.
Physics-based AI helps engineers predict process behavior without running a full simulation every time.
AI agents handle sequences of engineering tasks that once consumed hours.
And digital twins let teams test changes in a virtual environment before committing to physical trials.
Together, these capabilities describe an AI-defined fab: a semiconductor manufacturing factory where AI helps engineers optimize processes, catch problems earlier and make better decisions across the full manufacturing chip lifecycle.

items.t: Same Model, Different Harness: CUGA, Hermes, and Deep Agents — When to Pick CUGA?
items.x:
There are nearly 200 agent harnesses to choose from. We gave three of them the same open-weight model and 90 AppWorld tasks, and changing the harness moved task completion from 30% to 81%. For enterprise use, CUGA adds what this benchmark does not test: rules that the harness enforces and deployment inside your own boundary.
Community lists such as awesome-agent-harness and best-of-Agent-Harnesses track nearly 200 of them, and they make one point clearly: the harness matters, not only the model. In one analysis that best-of-Agent-Harnesses cites, the same GLM-5.2 model went from 23% to 52% on SWE-bench Pro when only the harness changed.
So the right question is not "which harness is best?" but "which harness fits my workload, with my model?" Hermes from Nous Research is built for always-on personal assistants, and Deep Agents from LangChain for long, multi-step tasks such as research. Both are excellent at those jobs.
Enterprise work is a different job. Agents act on business systems, such as CRM and payments, and they must follow rules that hold whatever the model decides. CUGA (ConfigUrable Generalist Agent) is IBM's open-source harness built for that job, with open-weight or hosted models, inside your own environment, including sovereign clouds and air-gapped deployments.

Apple is adjusting its App Store policies to make it more difficult for minors to use online dating apps or AI companions that engage in “sexual or romantic content,” the tech giant shared in an announcement to developers on Monday.

items.t: The 'Astra can read and write weights to improve Qwen' post is misleading
items.d: Article URL: https://honnibal.dev/blog/astra-read-write-misleading Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50351111 Points: 1038 # Comments: 209
items.x:
The experiments that read raw weights and the ones that fix Qwen use completely different techniques.
Stage magicians often do the same trick multiple ways. One iteration uses a gimmick prop, the next one shows you the prop isn’t gimmick but that one palms the object, the third time was a forced choice etc. When you watch the performance you assume there’s only one technique, so each time they do it they seem to debunk your hypothesis about how it must be working.
This is pretty much how the experiments in the ‘Astra can read and write weights to improve Qwen’ post work. The post’s abstract says:
Just by looking at the raw weights, GPT-6 Astra can tell what a network was trained to do. And without any environment feedback, it has no trouble writing, from scratch, small game-playing networks that outplay networks trained with PPO for 100 million steps.
Likewise, asked to make Qwen3.5-0.8B better at math without gradients, Astra identifies an issue in its weights causing reasoning loops that Qwen’s own model card warns about, and fixes this by natively editing 0.016% of the weights.

items.t: How “reverse game theory” could keep AI agents in check
items.d: A new approach known as “reverse game theory” aims to control powerful AI models by designing systems that incentivize them to stick to the rules. As AI models become more capable, safety researchers are scrambling to ensure they are…
items.x:
Rules over reasoning: Instead of trying to peer inside AI "brains" to ensure good behavior, a growing group of researchers wants to design incentive systems that make following the rules the most rational choice—regardless of what's actually happening under the hood.
Catching AI playing dumb: One proposed trick involves rewarding models not just for test performance, but for how well their answers predict what a second model would say—making deliberate underperformance a losing strategy.
Cops, citizens, and collusion: Princeton's Elad Hazan envisions AI models taking turns as "solvers" and "auditors," borrowing from human systems like law enforcement—though the risk of agents colluding remains a real and unsolved problem.
The market may be the biggest obstacle: Even a perfectly aligned AI could lose out if it's slower or costlier than a less scrupulous competitor—raising the uncomfortable question of whether the real mechanism in need of a redesign is the free market itself.

Now in beta: Apple's new Audio Intelligence features can help you remember what someone said or take notes on conversations.
Apple’s AI-powered “Audio Intelligence” technology for the Apple Watch is now rolling out into beta testing, initially for developers in the iOS 27.3 update, after first being announced at the company’s Surprise and Shine hardware event in September. The technology includes a set of four opt-in AI features that allow Apple Watch Series 12 wearers to detect important sounds, identify songs, catch up on conversations, and take notes.
The sound recognition feature will help deaf and hard-of-hearing users identify important sounds like sirens, alarms, or doorbells from their watch, while the song recognition feature taps into Apple’s Shazam app to detect music playing in the background and identify the song name and artist.
However, the more potentially controversial features are those that listen to human conversations: Live Rewind and Siri Recaps.
Given the backlash to AI recording devices, like Meta’s AI glasses and other AI wearables, Apple has attempted to carve out a space where the features can be useful to Apple Watch owners, while still respecting the privacy of those around them.

items.t: Cities Worldwide Build and Scale AI Services With NVIDIA Physical and Agentic AI
items.d: Cities generate enormous amounts of data from cameras, sensors and operational systems, but turning it into useful action — for planning, maintenance and public services — remains a challenge. Physical and agentic AI offer new ways to…
items.x:
Cities generate enormous amounts of data from cameras, sensors and operational systems, but turning it into useful action — for planning, maintenance and public services — remains a challenge.
Physical and agentic AI offer new ways to close that gap, from digital twins for infrastructure planning to vision and service agents, while keeping local governments in control of how sensitive data is processed and used.
Building on initiatives announced at GTC Berlin , NVIDIA and its partners are expanding physical AI and AI agents to cities worldwide. Shared computing infrastructure gives city departments, neighboring municipalities and local developers a common foundation to build on — extending services without each organization having to acquire and manage resources of their own.
From resident services to vision agents, cities are adopting NVIDIA agentic AI to deliver faster, more responsive public services.

items.t: Here’s who is falling in line for Trump’s “Super Intelligence” loyalty test
items.d: This story originally appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox first, sign up here. At the end of September, President Trump signed an executive order that contained just one directive…
items.x:
At the end of September, President Trump signed an executive order that contained just one directive, ordering government agencies to rebrand what they had been calling artificial intelligence as “Super Intelligence.” That term beat out other contenders, including “Extreme Intelligence” and “Supreme Intelligence,” offered by the president in a poll on X a couple of weeks earlier.
Rebrands are, of course, now a White House tradition: Trump has changed names to project US dominance of certain bodies of water (the Gulf of America and Lake America), to signal new institutional priorities (Department of War), or simply to leave his mark on storied places (see the ongoing fight over renaming the Kennedy Center).
The stated reason for this name change is that today’s AI systems “amplify human ingenuity” rather than merely “imitate” intelligence, and the government’s terminology should reflect that.

items.t: Google takes Dreambeans to India in bid to bring AI-generated personal stories to the masses
items.d: Google's Dreambeans, its latest AI experiment, now supports 13 Indian languages.
items.x:
Google's Dreambeans, its latest AI experiment, now supports 13 Indian languages.
Google has launched its experimental AI app Dreambeans in India, its first market outside the U.S., as the company looks to tap the world’s second-largest internet market to bring personalized visual stories drawn from users’ digital activity to a broader audience.
On Monday, Google expanded Dreambeans, available on Android and iOS, to India with support for 13 local languages, including Hindi, Punjabi, Tamil, Telugu, and Bengali, alongside English. The launch comes less than two months after Google made the app available to all eligible U.S. users aged 18 and older.
Introduced in June, Google’s Dreambeans uses information from connected Google services, including Calendar, Gemini, Gmail, Photos, Search, and YouTube, to proactively generate personalized, illustrated stories about users’ interests and everyday lives, without requiring them to enter a prompt.

items.t: Alibaba Cloud Model Studio Launches Memory, a Long-Term Memory Service for Personal Agents
items.d: Alibaba Cloud Model Studio's new Memory service gives personal agents long-term memory and user profiles, connects via API, MCP or CLI, and leads HaluMem and PersonaMem-v2 by its own count.
items.x:
Alibaba Cloud has launched Memory on its Model Studio platform, a long-term memory service built for personal AI agents, IT Home reported on November 2. The service lets agents remember a user's preferences, plans and earlier commitments across conversations, and assembles that history into a structured user profile that the agent can draw on later.
Alibaba Cloud says the system leads two public memory benchmarks. In charts released with the launch, where the system appears under the name Mementis, it ranks first on four HaluMem-medium factual-memory metrics, including recall, precision and F1, with a question-answering score of 85.15% against 81.71% for Zep, the next system listed. On the PersonaMem-v2 personalization benchmark it posts an overall score of 56.82, first among eight systems compared and highest on seven of nine tasks; MemBrain is second at 55.72. Alibaba Cloud notes that results for the other systems are taken from the OmniMemEval evaluation.

items.t: Tencent Hunyuan's Hyra 2.0 Research Agent Builds Its Own Tools for Proteins, Proofs and Chips
items.d: Tencent Hunyuan's Hyra 2.0 research agent now builds reusable tools, from a 57x-faster protein design model to force fields, a new quantum code and math results on Petty and Yau.
items.x:
Tencent Hunyuan has released Hyra 2.0, the second version of its autonomous research agent, on November 2. Where Hyra 1.0 focused on solving individual problems, including settling a sum-versus-difference exponent problem with the Hy3 model, the new version is designed to build reusable research tools. Results and code are published in an Apache 2.0 GitHub repository.
Hyra 2.0 runs as a three-layer system of overall, mission and worker agents, coordinated through a shared research board and a persistent task queue. A dedicated review worker checks outputs, agents keep layered memories, and a shared knowledge base distills lessons into reusable skills.
Tencent lists several tools the system produced. HyInv, an inverse protein-folding model with 1.96 million parameters, is said to run 57 times faster than ProteinMPNN with better structural agreement, designing 128 sequences in 50 milliseconds. HyPLM-Flash, a 650-million-parameter protein language model trained on 726 billion tokens, was the fastest of 12 models compared and ranked third on average across 35 tasks, processing about 130,000 residues per second on one H20.

items.t: Moore Threads' 2,112-GPU Wuxi Cluster Reaches 92.9% Utilization After Going Commercial
items.d: Moore Threads' MTT S5000 cluster in Wuxi runs 2,112 GPUs for 55 customers at 92.9% utilization, with DeepSeek V4 Flash inference tests reaching 92% of an H800 setup.
items.x:
A domestic computing cluster built on Moore Threads' MTT S5000 GPUs in Huishan, Wuxi, has moved from trial runs to commercial operation, according to a November 2 report by Zhidx. Planned at the 10,000-card scale, the Wuxi Huishan domestic computing center lit up its first phase in June, entered trial operation in July and began commercial service in October. The current phase runs 264 servers carrying 2,112 S5000 cards.
Figures shared with Zhidx put cluster utilization at 92.9%, with 55 customers and 33 models onboarded during the trial period. Training accounts for more than 62% of workloads, mixed training and inference for 14.7% and pure inference for 23.1%. The cluster is organized as four modules of roughly 500 cards each, was delivered turnkey, and reached full load within three months of going live. It supports more than 30 model families, including Qwen, GLM, DeepSeek, Kimi and MiniMax.
On inference, tests on the cluster's S5000 pool with DeepSeek V4 Flash at 7K input and 2K output tokens recorded single-machine output throughput of 994.97 tokens per second and effective output of 1,241 tokens per second. The system held 48 concurrent requests within its service-level target, which the report puts at 92% of an H800 setup under the same test.

Apple hinted at ways that it could spur revenue through third-party "opportunities" during its Monday night earnings call.
Apple’s services business remains at record levels, but it’s facing growing pressure. The central part of that business, Apple’s App Store, has faced regulatory pressure and a slump in mobile gaming, which have hurt services growth.
However, on Monday’s earnings call, Apple signaled that it may look to boost services revenue through third-party apps. What does that mean, exactly? Unfortunately, it’s not entirely clear.
When discussing how AI could potentially “contribute to revenue growth over time,” Kevan Parekh, Apple’s chief financial officer, said: “On the product side, you know, we feel AI offers a compelling reason for customers to upgrade and switch in order to get the latest capabilities, and we also feel there’s opportunities across third-party apps and partnerships as well as first-party opportunities.”
Parekh did not elaborate on what sorts of opportunities might be available via third-party apps.

On a new episode of Walter Isaacson’s podcast The Builders, set to publish on Tuesday, Tan put a price tag on his passion.
“I spend about maybe $100[,000] to $200,000 a year on tokens,” he told Isaacson. He uses agents for countless work projects and coding tasks and has freely shared his set of 23 Claude Code skills, called gstack, on GitHub — an effort to help teach others what agents can do, he said.
On the one hand, he uses his agent the way many people use AI: to help him research Isaacson’s podcast and prep for the kinds of questions he might be asked. On the other, his agent also helps him run his life.

items.t: CWE-bench v2: More coverage, quality, and transparency
items.x:
We’re on a journey to advance and democratize artificial intelligence through open source and open science.
CWE-bench is designed to test the limits of frontier cyber capabilities. In our continued pursuit to push the horizon at Collinear AI, CWE-bench v2 opens up a public set of 100 tasks that anyone can run and evaluate their models on. The setup is the same as before. An agent gets a checkout of a real open-source repository and a short instruction, with the goal of finding and fixing a security weakness without breaking existing functionality. Scoring is fully programmatic, so results are deterministic and anyone can reproduce them without extra cost. All our programmatic checks have been curated with the help of LLM judge panels that shape them towards the direction of hardness and fairness. We also maintain a held-out set, so that we can keep tracking progress on tasks no model has seen. To evaluate your model on the held-out set, contact cyber@collinear.ai.
Our goal is to be exhaustive. A defender has to anticipate the ways an attacker could get in, and get it right every single time. These 100 tasks cover 91 different CWEs, spanning a wide range of vulnerability classes.

items.t: Transformers Model Integration Contracts
items.x:
We’re on a journey to advance and democratize artificial intelligence through open source and open science.
On July 30, 2026, Transformers enabled PyTorch's scaled dot-product attention (SDPA) for T5. As a side effect, UMT5's decoder could attend to future tokens. During training, it could peek at the answer it was supposed to predict. Nothing crashed, and the bug stayed in main for almost two months.
When we later replayed those commits, a small UMT5 model running on CPU flagged it on every one of them. This post is about that model and the tests built around it.
Transformers supports over 750 model types, and its test suite is big: 88,000+ CPU tests on main, plus 200,000+ GPU tests in a daily run. Model tests are only part of it: we also test pipelines, training, distributed execution, quantization and attention kernels.
The integration tests load real checkpoints and exercise the model's API on real hardware. Running all of that on every PR would mean keeping a lot of GPUs busy all day long, which isn't practical. By the time a scheduled run finds a regression, it may already be in main.
Our approach is to shrink the model instead.

items.t: Trajectory raises $45M to make AI model training accessible to nontechnical experts
items.d: The one-year-old startup is now valued at $300 million.
items.x:
Whether developed by OpenAI, Anthropic, or built on open-source alternatives, current AI models share a critical limitation: they don’t learn from their mistakes without further training.
Businesses adapting these models for specialized fields, such as law and finance, typically get around this by fine-tuning general models. However, that often requires hiring internal research teams or relying on expensive consultants, commonly known as forward-deployed engineers (FDEs).
Trajectory, a startup founded about a year ago by three Stanford classmates with experience at Google DeepMind and Apple, wants to automate that process, allowing AI models to learn from feedback and continuously improve at specialized tasks.
The 18-person company just announced that it raised $45 million in a Series A round at a $300 million valuation, led by Sequoia, with participation from Nvidia, Bessemer Venture Partners, and Bain Capital Ventures.
Trajectory co-founder Ronak Malde compared foundational models to a very smart PhD student who’s always starting a new job. “But what the economy values is someone who worked on the job for 30 years,” he told TechCrunch.
The startup aims to solve this problem through an approach known as continual learning.

RSI is the point at which AI grows so good at training itself that it spawns a dramatic acceleration of AI capabilities. To the AI doomers, RSI represents the cataclysm from which there is no return.
While much attention has focused on the updated financials Anthropic revealed in its revised S-1A on Monday, (revenue is soaring, but so are expenses), the AI lab dropped another little bombshell in the fine print.
The filing seems to warn that the company is on the cusp of creating a model capable of recursive self-improvement (RSI).
To AI enthusiasts, RSI, or some version of AI reliably using itself to improve, represents the technology’s promise, where it becomes a tool of unimaginable productivity, scientific discovery, and more.
Anthropic seems to believe that RSI is both a promise and a peril. It says in the S-1 that it uses AI in its R&D, but it cautions: “Using AI to help build more capable AI could also pose a considerable safety risk, particularly if it sharply accelerates the pace of progress.

The website builder said that the job losses are part of a broader restructuring of its organization.
Squarespace, the web company that helps customers build and host their own websites, is laying off about one-fifth of its workforce, in a move that will affect hundreds of jobs.
Jeff Seedman, a public relations specialist representing Squarespace, confirmed the layoffs to TechCrunch. The Verge initially reported the layoffs.
“Squarespace is restructuring its organization and reducing its global workforce by approximately 19%, representing around 300 employees,” said Seedman. “The changes are intended to simplify how we operate, sharpen our priorities and enable the company to move faster as we position Squarespace for its next phase of growth.”
Website building has changed immensely over the last few years as a result of the generative AI boom. “Vibe-coding” website builders, which only require simple prompts from users to spin up functional front-end designs, have largely upended the industry, making it possible for users to create sites with significantly less effort.
These kinds of sites have become an increasingly central part of the website-building business. Last year, web host rival Wix bought Base44 for $80 million.

items.t: Astra can read and write weights to improve Qwen
items.d: Article URL: https://rikiyat.github.io/blog/weight-space-programming/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50341174 Points: 2956 # Comments: 897
items.x:
We find that frontier LLMs are surprisingly good at natively reading and writing neural network weights, well past what we’d expect from humans or conventional algorithms.
Just by looking at the raw weights, GPT-6 Astra can tell what a network was trained to do. And without any environment feedback, it has no trouble writing, from scratch, small game-playing networks that outplay networks trained with PPO for 100 million steps.
Likewise, asked to make Qwen3.5-0.8B better at math without gradients, Astra identifies an issue in its weights causing reasoning loops that Qwen’s own model card warns about, and fixes this by natively editing 0.016% of the weights. With the same sampling settings, this weight correction raises MATH-500 from 7.9% to 48.1% and generalizes out of the box to instruction following, raising IFEval by 3x.
All of this is possible without allowing Astra to write training loops. It uses its reasoning to figure out what each part of a neural network computes, or should compute, and changes the weights accordingly. We call this Weight-Space Programming.
Throughout the history of deep learning, we encoded our simplistic inductive biases into tiny symbolic optimizers like Adam or Muon.

items.t: Claude’s new rules against game cloning won’t stop the AI copying boom
items.d: The tsunami of imitators is way bigger than any one model maker can stem.
items.x:
Last week, Anthropic introduced a new system prompt designed to stop its Claude models from recreating specific, existing video games. But while that move could help shield Anthropic from some liability, it's unlikely to do much to slow a massive wave of AI-assisted game porting and copying that has emerged in recent months.
A social media user and AI decompilation enthusiast going by the name "chasm" was among the first to note the prompt change late last week, saying a new rule seemed to be added to the Claude Code prompt on or around October 27. That rule—included in a json file under the name "tengu_heron_brook"—reads as follows:
Do build original games, games in a genre, and games from the user’s own designs and assets. Don’t build a recreation of a specific existing game, even if it is renamed or called original.
XDA later independently verified that the new rule appears in version 2.1.314 of the Claude Code binary, which was released on October 30 . XDA also reported that the "tengu_heron_brook" rule had been used for other purposes in earlier versions and that the Claude Opus 5.5 model specifically seemed to have its own distinct and independent instructions restricting game recreations as part of its system prompt bundle.

items.t: Raising the quality of insights in agentic analytics
items.d: In just a few years, generative AI has changed the face of enterprise analytics, notably by making analytics accessible to users across the organization. Agentic AI promises to do even more, by automating entire workflows and taking…
items.x:
In just a few years, generative AI has changed the face of enterprise analytics, notably by making analytics accessible to users across the organization. Agentic AI promises to do even more, by automating entire workflows and taking actions based on agent insights. But there is a problem: The quality of insights that agents currently generate leaves much to be desired.
Fewer than half of agent-generated insights at the organizations surveyed for this report lead to business improvement. And while most respondents praise the quality of their agents’ descriptive insights, reviews of their prescriptive insights—those on which actions are based—are decidedly mixed.
Failure to produce insights that improve the business deprives organizations of their desired return on investment in agentic analytics. Worse, flawed insights that trigger incorrect actions can cause reputational or financial damage. This report gauges how companies view the quality of the outputs produced by their analytics agents and explores how organizations are seeking to boost insight quality and get their agents working harder for the business.

Agentic analytics is only just starting to deliver.

items.t: 42AI comes out of stealth with $62.5M and a world model that can ‘predict human behavior’

items.x:
Here's a question straight out of sci-fi: What if AI could predict what you were going to do before you decided to, even in a completely new situation?
Here’s a question straight out of sci-fi: What if AI could predict what you were going to do before you decided to, even in a completely new situation?
Israeli startup 42AI says it is developing a “behavioral world model” that can do just that, and it has just come out of stealth with $62.5 million in seed funding. The company is initially running its predictive system at a handful of financial brokerages, where it says the model can help predict how individual traders will respond to volatile conditions.
“Behavior is not deterministic; it’s constantly probabilistic,” 42AI’s CEO and co-founder Amit Gal-Or told TechCrunch when I asked him to justify his company’s tall claim. He argues that people have underlying psychological tendencies that influence their decisions even when their circumstances change, and that’s what the startup is trying to measure and convert into data that the model can understand.
“A week from now, you might be a different person, but your tendencies will always play out in certain areas to a probability or distribution,” his co-founder and CTO Ehud Ezra added.

Two startups tackling the data center water problem are joining forces in a $16 million deal.
US data centers use 17 to 19 billion gallons of water to cool their hot-running chips each year — and that number is expected to to triple in the next five years, according to the Water Foundation.
That’s an expensive and politically tricky proposition for investors throwing billions of dollars at the challenge of scaling up AI. One way to use less water is to do a better job monitoring the cooling fluids, a task that currently involves sending samples away to a laboratory for tests in a multi-day process.
Omen AI was founded in 2024 to solve that problem. The company is building a real-time sensor to determine whether valves were failing, or if bacteria growth in the system threatened to choke off water flow. After raising a $31 million Series A in June, Omen is now acquiring competitor Aquatic Labs in a $16 million cash-and-stock deal.
The deal came together after Omen founder Zach Laberge was introduced to Aquatic Labs’ CEO Allan Adams by an investor in the filtration space.

items.t: Stop counting tokens, start counting what ships
items.d: When a developer gives an AI agent a coding task, the agent does more than answer once. It plans, generates code, runs tests, and repeats the process to correct errors. A single task can use 10 to 50 times more tokens than a basic chat…
items.x:
When a developer gives an AI agent a coding task, the agent does more than answer once. It plans, generates code, runs tests, and repeats the process to correct errors. A single task can use 10 to 50 times more tokens than a basic chat prompt. The more useful the agent becomes, the more calls it makes. With per-token pricing, the workflows creating the most value can also become the most expensive.
The financial pressure is already visible. Uber reportedly exhausted its entire 2026 AI budget by April after expanding its use of Claude Code. GitHub Copilot moved from flat-rate pricing to metered credits. Gartner predicts that AI coding token costs will surpass average developer salaries by 2028.
The natural response is rationing usage caps, seat limits, and approvals before developers launch agents. But blanket limits can restrict the workflows delivering value. They also optimize the wrong number. Cost per token measures consumption, not results. Some spending reflects waste, including retries and runaway loops. Some represents the work of shipping software. A meter cannot distinguish them, and neither can a spending cap.
A better measure is cost per merged pull request: total AI-assisted development cost divided by the number of changes that pass review and are merged.

items.t: The agentic web is here
items.d: In 2001, a decade after he invented the World Wide Web, Tim Berners-Lee articulated a new vision. Together with two colleagues, he published an article in the magazine Scientific American in which he outlined what he called the “Semantic…
items.x:
In 2001, a decade after he invented the World Wide Web, Tim Berners-Lee articulated a new vision. Together with two colleagues, he published an article in the magazine Scientific American in which he outlined what he called the “Semantic Web” : an internet designed to be navigated by autonomous software agents that could address our every need, without requiring us to muck about with browsers and search engines ourselves.
To illustrate what this might look like, Berners-Lee and his colleagues told a story about a pair of siblings who use their agents to automatically research and book a physical therapy appointment for their mother, making sure it would be covered by insurance and fit their busy calendars.
At the turn of the millennium, this vision seemed far-fetched: Google had only been online for a couple of years, and most people were still on dial-up connections. But a quarter-century on, the dream of autonomous software agents that use the internet and carry out tasks for us has finally been realized. New tools such as Meta’s blockbuster Muse agent and OpenAI’s Dots are logging record downloads and being given access to people’s bank accounts and email inboxes, and Anthropic launched a research preview of its own Claude Duet agent in October.

items.t: Tencent Cloud Launches WAND-Vega as Its WAND Platform Generates 4.5 Million Images a Day
items.d: Tencent Cloud unveils WAND-Vega, Real-time Intelligence and a contact-center voice agent; WAND serves 2,000+ firms, making 4.5M images and 3M seconds of video daily.
items.x:
Tencent Cloud launched WAND-Vega, a multimodal application model, along with a real-time interaction service it calls Real-time Intelligence and an AI voice agent for its cloud contact center, at a multimodal session of the 2026 Tencent Global Digital Ecosystem Summit on October 30, IT Home reported, carrying Tencent's announcement.
WAND is Tencent Cloud's audio and video AI brand. It combines Hunyuan and other mainstream multimodal models, WAND-Vega and more than 100 media processing tools, covering generation, understanding, processing and encoding, and companies call it through existing cloud products and standard APIs. The upgraded WAND-Vega is built on mainstream open-source models that Tencent has heavily optimized. It generates and understands images, video and speech, and is tuned for advertising, e-commerce, short dramas and comics, and AI content tool platforms. The Hy Image 3.5 preview model released in September has also joined WAND for posters, storyboards and e-commerce visuals.
Tencent says WAND now serves more than 2,000 companies and generates more than 4.5 million images and 3 million seconds of video a day, cutting customers' overall content production costs by about 20%.

SenseTime has released SenseNova Loop-9B-Preview, an open-source multimodal model that uses repeated computation to extend its processing depth without duplicating the corresponding model weights. The release was announced on October 30.
The model accepts text and images and generates text for document understanding, coding, and tasks involving external tools. It runs a shared block of 24 decoder layers twice, creating a deeper computation path from a model with approximately nine billion parameters.
The documented training setup supports sequences of up to 262,144 tokens and combines text, images, code, and tool-use examples. SenseTime has published model weights, inference instructions, and training guidance, with the project distributed under the Apache 2.0 license. [ SenseTime ]

Meituan released LongCat-2.5 on November 2, adding stronger visual understanding and coding capabilities to its AI model lineup. The model has 1.6 trillion total parameters, with approximately 48 billion activated for each token, and is designed for tasks requiring sustained execution by AI agents.
The company said it expanded training on long task sequences and used large-scale reinforcement learning to improve work on complex codebases and complete software projects. It also converts failures encountered by real agents into reproducible training tasks to address gaps in model performance.
LongCat-2.5 processes visual and text inputs within a unified token framework, supporting visual coding, creative design, and 3D tasks. The model is available through Meituan’s online chat service and API platform, with GitHub and Hugging Face releases planned to follow. [ IT Home , in Chinese]

items.t: Qwen AI Glasses Add Call Translation and Media Translation in New OTA Update
items.d: Qwen AI Glasses gain real-time call translation for phone calls and meetings, media translation shown in the companion app, and better speech recognition in noisy places.
items.x:
Alibaba's Qwen AI Glasses received an over-the-air update on November 1 that adds call translation and media translation and improves noise handling, IT Home reported. The Qwen AI Glasses account had announced the update on Weibo on October 30.
Call translation provides real-time translation across languages during phone calls and online meetings, aimed at conversations with people abroad. Media translation covers content such as overseas podcasts, foreign-language online classes and foreign films. The glasses translate the audio in real time, and the translated text appears in sync in the Qwen AI wearables app on the user's phone, so the glasses handle listening while the phone acts as the screen.
The third change is better noise resistance. The update improves speech recognition in noisy environments, which the company says makes simultaneous interpretation more accurate and more timely. Clear audio pickup is the step most translation features depend on, especially in streaming settings such as calls, where speakers do not pause for the system to catch up.
The announcement did not say which models receive the update or which languages the new features support.
The update lands on a lineup that has grown quickly this year.

items.t: CCID Says China's AI Inference Data Has Overtaken Training Data, With 175 Trillion Daily Token Calls
items.d: CCID says AI inference data in China has overtaken training data for the first time, with daily token calls above 175 trillion as of June, more than 1,000 times the early-2024 level.
items.x:
The volume of data used for AI inference in China has surpassed the volume used for training for the first time, according to a report released on October 31 by the China Center for Information Industry Development (CCID), a research institute under the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology. CCTV News reported the finding on November 1, as carried by IT Home. CCID says the shift marks China's move from a stage focused on training and developing models to one of large-scale industrial use.
The report, a list of ten trends in what CCID calls new-domain, new-quality innovation, puts daily token calls in China at more than 175 trillion as of June 2026. That is more than 1,000 times the level at the start of 2024. CCID also says the iteration cycle of leading large models has shrunk from several months to a few weeks, or even a few days. In its words, AI is moving from a lab stage of feeding models to an industrial stage of using them.
The report ties this to manufacturing. Under China's AI Plus Manufacturing initiative, more than 500 excellence-level smart factories have been built across 31 provincial-level regions, covering more than 80% of the major categories of manufacturing.

items.t: Meituan Releases LongCat-2.5, a 1.6T Native Multimodal Model Built for Long-Horizon Agentic Coding
items.d: Meituan's LongCat-2.5 is a 1.6T native multimodal model with about 48B active per token, trained with long-horizon RL for agentic coding and optimized for W4A4 inference on domestic compute.
items.x:
Meituan's LongCat team released LongCat-2.5 on November 2, a native multimodal model built for long-horizon agent tasks, IT Home reported. The model has 1.6 trillion total parameters and activates about 48 billion of them per token. It builds on LongCat-2.0 and strengthens two things in particular: native visual understanding and agentic coding. The official release follows LongCat-2.5-Preview, which went live on the LongCat API platform on September 25.
Most of the training work targets long tasks. Meituan says it added more long-horizon trajectory data to long-sequence training and used large-scale long-horizon reinforcement learning to improve end-to-end engineering work, such as developing inside complex codebases and building complete projects. The team keeps expanding data synthesis, environment construction and mixed training across different agent harnesses. It also turns the failure trajectories of real agents into reproducible, verifiable training tasks, so it can keep adding data where the model is weak.
On the vision side, LongCat-2.5 represents visual signals as multi-level discrete tokens, so the backbone processes images and text in the same token form.

items.t: Progress on provable inference for large language models
items.d: We have made progress on a type of cryptographic proof known as a “zkSNARK.” In this post, we share some of that progress, primarily through a system we call FlashProve.
items.x:
Sharing progress on a powerful type of cryptographic proof known as a zkSNARK, which is uniquely fit for provable inference.
Roy Rinberg (Anthropic), Alex Allain (Anthropic); Alessandro Chiesa (EPFL, StarkWare), Miranda Christ (MIT, RESI), Rahul Dalal (Anthropic STEM Fellows Program, Succinct), Giacomo Fenzi (EPFL), Ben Mayer (Anthropic Fellows Program, MIT), Guy Weissenberg (EPFL)
When you talk to a friend in person, you have many ways to know it is really them: you can see them, hear them, shake their hand. When you talk to an AI model, you have almost none. A user querying a model today cannot check that the responses came from the specific model that a developer claims is responding, as opposed to one secretly substituted in by a routing service for cost reasons, or even by an attacker who has tampered with the token stream. Judging from the model’s output alone is unreliable, even if it produces high-quality responses. Cryptographic proofs of inference solve this problem: they let a model provider commit to a model and then prove that each response was produced by that model.

items.t: Make long-running agents faster with message threads
items.d: New in the Messages API, send your conversation once, and the API receives only what’s new with every turn.
items.x:
New in the Messages API, send your conversation once, and the API receives only what’s new with every turn.
Message threads is now available in public beta on the Claude Platform. With message threads, agents no longer need to resend the full conversation history on every turn, reducing latency for long-running sessions.
A coding agent might make hundreds of requests in one session, and each request resends every earlier message and tool result. Once a conversation reaches hundreds of thousands of tokens, resending all of it adds time before Claude starts responding. With message threads, agents send only what’s new since the last turn, which reduces time to first token (TTFT).
With message threads on by default for most Claude Code users, requests with 500k to 1M tokens see median TTFT drop by about 35%.
To use message threads, add the thread parameter to Messages API requests. The first request includes the full conversation and starts a thread. Each request after that includes only the new messages and the ID of the previous response. Between turns, we hold each thread in memory, where it’s encrypted and not written to disk. A thread expires 5 minutes after its last request and your client then resends the full conversation to start a new one.

Dazzle AI CEO Marissa Mayer recently became the latest tech CEO to face criticism over seemingly out-of-touch comments extolling the usefulness of AI.
In Mayer’s case, that involved asking an AI tool for help with a school-assigned description of her daughter. For OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, that’s included suggesting that parents create personalized podcasts for their kids’ drive to school and also declaring that he could not imagine parenting without ChatGPT. Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg has even suggested that it will become increasingly acceptable to meet your social and romantic needs through AI.

items.t: AI Agents Now Create Over 20,000 Tencent Cloud TDSQL-C Databases a Day, Up More Than 80x
items.d: Tencent Cloud says agents now create over 20,000 TDSQL-C database instances a day, with over 1 million active. WorkBuddy user Li Ning runs about 50 agents and plans to reach 200 within a year.
items.x:
AI agents now create more than 20,000 Tencent Cloud TDSQL-C database instances a day, a rate that has grown more than 80-fold over the past year, Tencent Cloud said on October 30 at the AI-native database session of the 2026 Tencent Global Digital Ecosystem Summit, IT Home reported. More than one million agent-created instances are now active.
A Tencent Cloud vice president described the change this way: the database's first user has changed, but its first responsibility has not. While building an app, an agent needs to create a database quickly and test changes in an isolated environment. Once the app goes live, the database has to scale with the workload without disrupting the business.
To support this, TDSQL-C has upgraded its serverless scaling and added database branching. Branching lets an agent test a new approach on a separate copy of the database before releasing it. In a stress test, the serverless version scaled from 0.25 to 32 compute units in 75 seconds and dropped back to 0.25 within 10 seconds after the load ended. TDSQL-C is also integrated with CloudBase, so an agent can create tables, set permissions and generate APIs while it builds an app. The PostgreSQL edition of CloudBase is fully compatible with Supabase.

items.t: DeepSeek Harness Team Open-Sources a Super-agent Prototype That Finds and Fixes Bugs on Its Own
items.d: DeepSeek's Harness team released an MIT-licensed Super-agent prototype: a resident Router dispatches work to isolated Workers that react to GitHub and chat events, fix bugs and open PRs.
items.x:
The DeepSeek Harness team on the evening of October 31 published a design write-up on what it calls a Super-agent, an always-on agent that pushes several tasks forward at once, looks for work on its own and recovers from faults, and released a companion research prototype on GitHub under the MIT license, Chinese tech media reported.
The repository, dsh-superagent-prototype, packages a proactive coding agent for a single GitHub repository as a bundle for DeepSeek Harness. It listens to GitHub and, optionally, Feishu. When an allowed user asks for work, it opens a work item, handles it in its own session and directory, and replies in the original conversation, for example with a pull request. The README stresses that this is research code rather than an official DeepSeek product, and that some designs in the write-up are not implemented.
The system is event-driven: chat messages, emails, review comments and CI results arrive as triggers, filtered first by deterministic code and then by a model. The team also separates agent state from execution environments so the agent can stay online in the cloud while reaching a user's own machines, and runs an external Watchdog session that checks whether Workers are making real progress.

A federal judge denied a motion by xAI seeking to dismiss an NAACP lawsuit accusing the SpaceX-owned company of failing to obtain permits needed to operate the gas turbines powering its Colossus data center outside Memphis.
Suing on behalf of the NAACP, the Southern Environmental Law Center said the AI company had “installed and operated at least 35 combustion turbines and other sources of air pollution at the Colossus site without ever obtaining the necessary preconstruction or operating air permits.” It also accused xAI of violating the Clean Air Act.

items.d: OpenAI’s latest funding round doesn't seem to be living up to expectations.
items.x:
OpenAI’s latest funding round doesn't seem to be living up to expectations.
OpenAI’s latest funding round isn’t quite living up to expectations, according to multiple news reports.
OpenAI was previously reported to be raising $30 billion at a $1.4 trillion valuation, and then at a $1.25 trillion valuation, ahead of a planned IPO. But The Financial Times reported Friday that the company has subsequently lowered its funding target to $20 billion, with a first close that’s expected to be even lower than that.
The round will be led by a group of investors from the United Arab Emirates, the FT said. A subsequent retail offering for wealthy individuals could bring the total funding amount to the $20 billion target.
A follow-up story in The Wall Street Journal offered more details, namely that the company has secured $11 billion so far, and that its fundraising efforts had met with a “tepid” response from some large investors.
TechCrunch has reached out to OpenAI for comment. The company’s reported funding challenges could be blamed, in part, on bad timing, as Wall Street investors have become wary of heavy AI infrastructure spending, leading to a major sell off of tech stocks.

items.x:
Recursive self-improvement, AI that helps build the next AI, has become one of the most visible themes among Chinese model developers this autumn. A Leiphone survey of recent disclosures finds a common pattern: no one is letting AI rewrite model weights. Instead, labs point AI at training pipelines, inference systems, GPU kernels, sandboxes and agent harnesses.
A September paper by 35 researchers from Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Tsinghua, ByteDance, SenseTime and others, The Last AI Built by Humans, proposes five levels of self-improvement and places most frontier systems between levels one and two.
Zhipu has the clearest production case. An Infra Agent driven by GLM-5.3 built the serving stack for GLM-5.3-Flash on a cluster of about 100,000 China-made accelerators in two weeks, storing working fixes as reusable templates. Its HarnessPro paper with Tsinghua then had agents rewrite their own harness.
DeepSeek started with the training ground. Its DSec cluster, built with Tsinghua, produces about 3 million sandboxes a day, so agents can build environments that train stronger agents. DeepSeek Harness treats tools and even its core runtime as plug-ins that can be swapped without a restart and rolled back.

items.t: Tsinghua and Zhipu's HarnessPro Lets Agents Rewrite Their Own Harness, Cutting Task Costs 26%
items.d: HarnessPro, from Tsinghua, Zhipu and partners, has agents study their own runs and rewrite their harness without reference answers, raising pass rates 2 points and cutting cost per task 26.1%.
items.x:
Researchers from Tsinghua University, Zhipu, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, the University of Warwick and Kuaishou have released HarnessPro, a method that lets an AI agent improve the harness it runs in, the framework that sets its prompts, tools, budgets and task flow. The paper, posted to arXiv on October 19 with Zhipu chief scientist Tang Jie among the authors, adds a second goal to self-improvement: performance should go up while execution cost comes down. The code is on GitHub.
The work follows Zhipu's September account of an Infra Agent powered by GLM-5.3 that helped build and tune the inference infrastructure for GLM-5.3-Flash, raising end-to-end throughput to about three times the initial baseline in under two weeks.
HarnessPro starts by running the existing harness and collecting tool calls, environment feedback and token use. A trajectory analysis agent reviews several runs of the same task to find causes of failure as well as waste such as repeated searches, aimless exploration and redundant checks.

items.t: China Southern Power Grid and Huawei Sign Deeper Pact on AI, Compute and Power IoT OS Dianhong
items.d: China Southern Power Grid and Huawei signed a deeper strategic cooperation agreement on October 27 covering power-carbon-compute coordination, AI, the Dianhong power IoT OS and the industry ecosystem.
items.x:
China Southern Power Grid and Huawei signed a comprehensive agreement to deepen their strategic cooperation in Shenzhen on October 27, Huawei announced on October 29, as reported by IT Home. The grid operator's chairman, Qian Chaoyang, and Huawei deputy chairman and rotating chairman Wang Tao held talks and witnessed the signing.
The two sides will focus on four areas: coordination of power, carbon and computing, AI applications, Power HarmonyOS, and building the industry ecosystem. The work targets the country's push for a new energy system, a new power system and new grid construction, and the coordinated development of six networks: water, the new grid, computing, next-generation communications, urban underground pipelines and logistics.
The partnership builds on an operating system launched in 2023. That year, China Southern Power Grid and the OpenAtom Foundation, with Huawei's support, released Dianhong, described as the country's first power IoT operating system. Built on OpenHarmony and openEuler, it lets a single system run across different types and brands of power equipment, with plug-and-play devices and shared data.

items.t: Tencent Map Opens Its Agent Capabilities to Developers Through MCP, Agent Skills and Connectors
items.d: Tencent Map laid out its agent stack, opening route planning, place search and ride-hailing to developers via MCP, Agent Skills and connectors, and launched LBSwork, a desktop AI map workbench.

Tencent presented a full map of the agent capabilities in Tencent Map at a Tencent Map industry session during the 2026 Tencent Global Digital Ecosystem Summit in Shenzhen on October 30, IT Home reported. The company said it is opening these map agent capabilities to industry customers, smart hardware makers and developers.
Several products already use them. They include the Yuanbao assistant, Xiaowei inside WeChat, OPPO's Breeno assistant, Rokid AI glasses and AI wearables from Guangfan. In Yuanbao, a single sentence can trigger route planning, and one-sentence ride-hailing is due to launch soon. Through Xiaowei, a user who sees a store recommendation in a WeChat Channels video can ask where the physical shop is and get an answer on the spot.
For cars, Tencent built a vehicle map agent made up of five agents that handle trip planning, map rendering, ecosystem content, intelligent navigation and parking guidance.

items.t: Lenovo Brings Tianxi AI 4.5 to AI PCs, Letting Phones and Tablets Hand Off Tasks to a Desktop
items.d: Lenovo released Tianxi AI 4.5 for AI PCs, adding a Super Mode that acts across apps, an AI note-taker that joins brainstorms, and remote task handoff from phones and tablets to a PC.
items.x:
Lenovo released Tianxi AI 4.5, its personal AI agent, on AI PCs on October 30, according to a Lenovo-supplied article republished by QbitAI. The PC release follows the phone version on October 20 and the tablet version on October 27, so the update now covers all three device types. Lenovo pitches this version at office workers, with upgrades for office tasks, meetings and business travel.
The centerpiece is a new Super Mode that moves the assistant from answering questions to carrying out tasks. Tianxi AI 4.5 adds connectors for Feishu, the Lenovo Browser and WeCom and links them with a personal knowledge base, so local files and cloud documents can be used together. A single instruction can trigger the assistant to break down and complete a multi-step job across apps, such as checking meetings, assigning tasks or searching material and sending a group notice. A skills marketplace bundles connectors, multi-task collaboration and skills, including improved slide generation, and a system-control skill pack can adjust graphics, power and system settings on request.
For meetings, the AI note-taker was rebuilt. It provides real-time transcription with subtitles and can take part in brainstorming as a participant, offering its own views and ideas.

items.t: Tencent Cloud Launches Data and Training Stack for Robots and Self-Driving, Plans TCLake XPhysis
items.d: Tencent Cloud launched an integrated multimodal data processing and model training stack for embodied AI and autonomous driving, and said it will release a TCLake XPhysis physical AI platform.
items.x:
Tencent Cloud launched an integrated multimodal data processing and model training and inference solution for physical AI applications such as embodied intelligence and autonomous driving at the big data session of the 2026 Tencent Global Digital Ecosystem Summit on October 30. It also announced it will release TCLake XPhysis, a platform covering the full physical AI engineering chain.
Robots and self-driving systems generate huge volumes of video and sensor data and improve through repeated training and simulation. Tencent Cloud says these jobs have typically been spread across several sets of tools, leading to duplicated data preparation and hard-to-reuse assets. Its new solution uses DataBuddy workflows and the AI DLC data lake compute service to put data management, development orchestration and model jobs on one platform, linking data processing, training, inference and simulation validation.
Within the stack, Xpark and Meson handle multimodal data cleaning, quality checks, labeling and sample preparation. TCRay provides distributed training and inference, and TCLake manages data and AI assets in one place.

items.t: InSpatio Opens a Simulation-First Robot Data Center in Hangzhou, Targets a Million Hours a Month
items.d: Spatial intelligence firm InSpatio opened what it calls China's first simulation-led embodied AI data center in Hangzhou, aiming to produce a million hours of robot training data a month.
items.x:
InSpatio, a spatial intelligence foundation model company spun out of SenseTime in 2025, opened what it describes as China's first simulation-led data collection center for embodied AI in Hangzhou on October 29, according to Leiphone. The center aims to produce data at a scale of a million hours a month, or about 100,000 hours a day.
InSpatio's argument is that robots lack not only data volume but variety. A robot can grasp reliably at a fixed shelf, yet success drops when the shelf turns, another row of drinks blocks the target or the robot has to reach from the other side. According to the China Academy of Information and Communications Technology, more than 70 robot training grounds were operating in China by the end of June, with more than 40 more planned, but many focus on easy-to-show tasks such as folding clothes and tidying tables. Each new layout means rebooking a site and operators, so costs grow with every change.
InSpatio's approach changes the formula from people times hours to environment configurations times parallel compute.

items.t: Baidu Says Search Now Improves Itself From Live Feedback, Cuts API to 4.9 Yuan per 1,000 Calls
items.d: Baidu says its search engine now retrains itself from real queries and feedback without human tuning, and is selling an enhanced search AI API at 4.9 yuan per 1,000 calls through December 31.
items.x:
Baidu said at a product briefing for the Baidu app in Beijing on October 30 that its search engine has achieved what it calls recursive self-evolution, and it launched an upgraded search AI API with a promotional price that it says undercuts DeepSeek's search API.
Baidu describes the self-evolution as a closed loop of retrieval, feedback and retraining. Every real search and the user feedback that follows are turned into training signals and fed back into the system, so the models keep iterating without manual intervention. Baidu says multiple agents improve together through this online feedback loop and that overall iteration efficiency is up more than 80 percent. The company did not publish independent evaluations of the claim.
The API sits on what Baidu calls a four-layer AI-native architecture. The content layer draws on more than 80 languages and an index of hundreds of billions of quality pages, with data credibility said to be up more than 50 percent. The engine layer is where the self-evolution runs. The architecture layer handles high concurrency and low latency for enterprise use. The application layer supports access through an API, MCP and skills.

items.t: Nvidia weighs playing the cosigner for Nscale’s AI data center in West Virginia
items.d: When investors get nervous about AI spending, it helps to have the chipmaker that sells the chips offer to cosign the loan.
items.x:
When investors get nervous about AI spending, it helps to have the chipmaker that sells the chips offer to cosign the loan.
Nvidia is in talks to guarantee billions in debt financing for AI cloud provider Nscale’s planned Anthropic data center in West Virginia, The Information reported Thursday. Bloomberg later corroborated the report. Anthropic has signed a $44.6 billion contract for the project’s first building alone, according to Nscale’s IPO filing. In essence, the chipmaker would be co-signing a customer’s loans, a sign of how hard the AI industry is working to keep its buildout plans afloat as investors grow jittery about the amounts of money involved.
The proposed arrangement would help Nscale secure financing for the electricity and construction costs of its West Virginia campus.

items.t: Ollie, a privacy-focused AI assistant, is shutting down
items.d: As an increasing number of AI assistants flood the market, the founder of Ollie, an assistant that respected its users' privacy, says it will be shutting down in a week.
items.x:
As an increasing number of AI assistants flood the market, the founder of Ollie, an assistant that respected its users' privacy, says it will be shutting down in a week.
Ollie, a startup whose mission was to deliver an AI assistant that respected its users’ privacy, says that it will be shutting down in a week. Bill Lennon, the company’s co-founder and CEO, took to X on Friday to deliver the news, noting that the app will officially shut down on November 6.
“I’m really proud of what we accomplished,” Lennon said. “We built an incredible personal assistant with a small team, and learned a ton. I’m grateful to our amazing team, our users, our investors, and everyone who supported us on this journey.”
The text-based AI assistant market has exploded over the past year, as the increasingly powerful models that undergird such applications have made them significantly more useful for daily tasks.
Ollie, which discussed its $7.5 million seed round led from Khosla Ventures with TechCrunch in September, offered a subscription-based model. The assistant was focused on helping families stay connected and organized. The app connected to a user’s email and calendar, while also providing integrated functions to help with appointment bookings, meal planning, and bill payments.

items.d: Intel is being hurt by PC sales as the AI industry gobbles memory and other components causing PC prices to rise.

Intel is being hurt by PC sales as the AI industry gobbles memory and other components causing PC prices to rise.
Intel’s stock suffered one of its worst days ever on Friday, crashing around 28% after the chip giant reported a weaker-than-expected outlook for the fourth quarter.
This route reduced the value of Intel’s holdings by the government by $12 billion, CNBC reports. The Trump administration had the government buy 10% stake over a year ago. Nvidia, which also took a big stake in Intel in 2025, saw its stock drop a bit on Friday as well. Much of the tech industry — especially chipmakers — were caught in the selloff.

items.t: Anthropic expected to receive high ‘junk’ rating from credit agencies following IPO, FT report says
items.d: Blackstone's forecast is just a prediction, but naturally, a high junk rating would make it more difficult and costlier for Anthropic to raise the money to keep funding its massive spending that has undergirded its business.
items.x:
The new report says the AI lab will likely qualify for a high junk rating.
Anthropic is expected to receive a high “junk” rating from credit rating agencies following its initial public offering, according to a report from the Financial Times.
The FT says the investment giant Blackstone, the investment giant and anchor investor in a recent $63 billion deal to finance Anthropic’s chips, told investors in the deal that it expects the AI lab to receive a “high” junk rating after its IPO. Previously, the FT notes, Blackstone had said the opposite: that the Claude-maker would receive an investment-grade rating (indicating low risk for lenders) before 2027 rolls around.
Now, Blackstone expects double B range rating, the top tier of speculative “junk” grade, according to the reporting.
TechCrunch reached out to Anthropic and Blackstone but both declined to comment.
Blackstone’s forecast is just a prediction, but naturally, a high junk rating would make it more difficult and costlier for Anthropic to raise the money to keep funding its massive spending that has undergirded its business.
